Not ported (and why): `PQSMeshPlanet.cs` / `PQSMeshWrapper.cs` (editor tools, referenced nowhere in Assembly-CSharp), `PQS.CreateMaps` / `BilinearInterp*` (editor map baking, Texture2D sampling), materials / renderers / shadows (`ApplyTerrainShaderSettings`, AssignQuad's renderer setup), the floating-origin machinery (`LocalSpacePQStorage`, `FastUpdate*` / `PreciseUpdate*QuadsPosition`), PQS_Collider*, PQS_PartCollider, PQSMod_CreateSphereCollider, SurfaceObject / PQSSurfaceObject / PQSMod_SurfaceObjectQuads / SpaceCenterSurfaceObject (WP-12b and scene glue), PQSLandControl's colour / scatter half and the other colour / scatter / material mods (WP-11 deferred them; WP-12c).

### Exact / approximate / changed

| # | item | class | detail / measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | quad mesh vertices with `surfaceRelativeQuads` | changed (frame) | KSP: `quad.transform.InverseTransformPoint(sphere.transform.TransformPoint((Vector3)vertRel))` through the floating-origin world pose (float noise ~1e-2 m that depends on the scene origin). Core: the sphere's frame is the body-fixed frame, so it is `(Vector3)vertRel - (Vector3)positionPlanet` with `meshOrigin = (Vector3)positionPlanet` widened: KSP's own float quantisation of the planet-relative vertex (1/16 m at Kerbin's radius), no world-pose noise. The exact double vertices are kept in `PQ::vertsD`. Max |origin + float vertex - double vertex| on synth_a: 0.031 m |
| 2 | target position | changed (precision) | KSP: `transform.InverseTransformPoint(target.position)` in float world space; core: the host's body-fixed double |
| 3 | floating-origin quad moves | changed (dropped) | no floating origin in the core (PHYSICS-SPIKE.md lever 1) |
| 4 | `Time.realtimeSinceStartup` | model | injectable; default a constant 1 s = a running game on an infinitely fast machine: UpdateQuadsInit's pass is out of time as in KSP (maxFrameEnd is still 0 there, so that pass never subdivides), UpdateQuads never is |
| 5 | pool | exact | fresh quads materialise on first GetQuad (KSP allocates 9,216 GameObjects up front): fresh quads are interchangeable and always below the reused ones on the Stack, and each copies the static arrays as they were at IncreasePQCache, as in C# |
| 6 | `PQSHeightWorkers` (parallel height pass, opt-in: `PQS::heightWorkers`) | exact (bit-identical, gated) | the height pass of quads about to be built (UpdateQuadsInit's visible leaves, Subdivide's visible children) runs on independent spheres with the same stack; BuildQuad takes vertHeight, the vertColor components the height mods wrote (NaN sentinel) and allowScatter per vertex and still computes the map coordinates. Assumes no height depends on mod scratch carried from an earlier evaluation (true for every stock mod; the replays and the capture check pass with workers) |
| 7 | coroutines | model | `StopCoroutine("UpdateSphere")` does not stop a coroutine started from an IEnumerator (Unity's documented rule), so a reset + restart within one frame leaves two UpdateSphere loops; kept. UNVERIFIED against the game |
| 8 | `Mesh.RecalculateBounds` | native, UNVERIFIED | AABB min / max, center = (max + min) * 0.5, extents = (max - min) * 0.5 in float; not part of the gated vertex data |
| 9 | `WaitForSeconds(frameTimeDelta)` | model | resumes on the first frame with `realtimeSinceStartup` >= start + delta (Unity uses scaled time); only with frameTimeDelta > 0 (Reset default 0) |

### Performance (Ryzen 9 7950X3D, `build/RelWithDebInfo/tests/wp12_bench.exe 3` pinned to one CCD with `start /affinity`; the frequency CCD (logical CPUs 16-31) is ~1.5x faster on this workload than the V-cache CCD (0-15); unpinned runs land anywhere in between)

| | stock Kerbin (KSC pad) | stock Mun | flat stack (one constant-height mod) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BuildQuad per quad, 1 thread (every built leaf rebuilt 3 x), frequency CCD / V-cache CCD | 0.64 / 1.03 ms (heights alone 0.60 / 0.92 ms) | 0.75 / 1.28 ms (heights 0.73 / 1.30 ms) | 24 / 37 us |
| of which the WP-12a geometry (build - heights): directions, positions, normals, edge-normal backup, tangents, channels, mod hooks | ~20-40 us (Kerbin, Mun) | | 22 / 34 us |
| StartSphere (tree + every initially visible quad: 479 / 417 builds), 1 thread, frequency CCD | 308 ms | 332 ms | 9.5 ms |
| StartSphere with 2 / 4 / 8 / 15 height workers (frequency CCD) | 199 / 143 / 116 / 108 ms (2.9x) | - / 166 / - / 90 ms (3.7x) | - |
| steady frame at rest (FixedUpdate + FrameUpdate: UpdateVisual, UpdateQuads, stitching) | 0.018-0.032 ms | 0.027-0.030 ms | 0.001 ms |

The height stack (WP-11) is 90-97 % of a quad build; the quadtree and the WP-12a build code cost ~20-40 us per quad and ~0.03 ms per steady frame. The workers cut the scene-load build ~3-3.7x within one CCD; what remains serial is the build pass of the ~480 quads outside the height pass (geometry, stitching, tangents, the UV pass: ~25 ms), the 10 UpdateQuadsInit passes, and the builds outside the predicted batches (76 of 479 on Kerbin: neighbour / corner builds, single-child subdivisions). KSP itself spreads this work over frames through maxFrameTime; these numbers are one call's wall time.

An in-game capture of the quad set (`quad_subdivision`, PHYSICS-SPIKE.md section 7): per PQ under Kerbin's PQS from a fixed vessel at the pad: name, subdivision, isVisible, edgeState, gcDist, positionPlanet, and for a few quads the mesh vertices / normals / tangents / uv / uv2. That would check the LOD fixtures, the TRS-based directions and normals in the game itself (today they are checked against the natives' capture rows and the independent reference).

### Quirks reproduced (a later implementer must keep them)

1. `PQS.UpdateQuads` sorts the six roots by distance and updates only the first five (`Mathf.Min(quads.Length, 5)`).
2. `UpdateQuadsInit` always runs ten passes (quadCount is only ever 6), and its building pass is out of time in the game (maxFrameEnd = 0), so it never subdivides; leaves below minLevel are still subdivided there.
3. `PQSMod_QuadEnhanceCoast` compares heights above the radius (meshVertMin / Max) with `radius + coastLessThan`: every real quad takes the ocean branch, and the stock oceanFactor is 1.0, so the mod does nothing in the stock game.
4. `PQSMod_UVPlanetRelativePosition.OnQuadBuilt` rewrites the STATIC `PQS.cacheUVs`, which is why BuildMeshUVChannel assigns cacheUVs and the `uvs` scratch that BuildVertexSphereUV / QuadUV write is never assigned to any mesh; uv2.y uses `quad.vertNormals`, which sphere-normal stacks never write (stale pool contents).
5. A fresh pooled quad's MeshRenderer is enabled: an assigned, never-built invisible quad keeps `rendererEnabled` (KSP draws its 1 m template grid); the C ABI and the handoff test draw only built quads.
6. `PQSCache.DestroyQuad` keeps a quad's mesh, normals, edge normals, edgeState, isCached, meshVertMin / Max and delegates; `GetRightmostCornerNormal` can read the edge normals of a subdivided (not rebuilt) quad.
7. `PQSCache.PQSGlobalPresetList.SetPreset(string)` compares with the CURRENT preset and renames inside the loop: from "Default", "Low" keeps index 1, "High" gets 2.
8. `UpdateVisual` reads `Time.realtimeSinceStartup` twice for the fixed-frame timing.
9. The quad build's heights depend on the quad (OnQuadPreBuild: MapDecal / FlattenArea quadActive from the quad centre), the public GetSurfaceHeight on whether any quad was ever built (OnQuadBuilt).
10. `PQSMod_CelestialBodyTransform.OnSetup` sets forceActivate when no CelestialBody is found (a height-only stock sphere without a host therefore force-activates).

### Findings (KSP behaviours the tests pin down; all ported as they are)

- `ModuleGroundPart.UpdateModuleUI` is private and non-virtual; `ModuleGroundSciencePart` declares its own virtual of the same name, so the base class's own calls never reach the science / experiment UI (kept: `UpdateGroundModuleUI` vs `UpdateModuleUI`).
- `ModuleGroundPart.OnPartUnpack` re-enables the part's `ModuleAnimationGroup` while the part is being deployed (`beingDeployed`) even if it was disabled.
- A part with `kinematicDelay < 1` that is being deployed waits 3 s (the field is overwritten with 3) and then needs `GroundContact`; without it the part shows "cannot deploy unless on the ground" and stays `beingDeployed`.
- `ROCManager.ValidateCBBiomeCombos` indexes `myCelestialBodies[num2]` after `RemoveAt(num2)`: a definition whose last body entry is an unknown body throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (tested as `std::out_of_range`).
- `ROCManager.Start` keeps a definition whose prefab is missing (warning only) and drops one whose prefab has no ROC component.
- `ROCScenario.Instance` is never assigned (only set to null): always null (kept).
- `LandClassROC.AddScatterMeshController` draws `Random.Range(1, (int)num2)` even for quads with no ROC; with `num = 0` (`1/0 = inf`) `(int)inf = int.MinValue` and the draw takes the `max < min` branch.
- `DeployedScienceExperiment.ProcessSeismicEvent` returns without clearing the part list or the pending flag when the impact is below `MinimumSeismicEnergyRequired`: the event stays pending and no further callback is scheduled until a power-state change.
- `CalculateScience` always fires `onGroundScienceGenerated`, also with `num = 0` (the toggles of a part call it with dt = 0).
- A new `DeployedScienceCluster` / `Part` / `Experiment` subscribes in `Start` (next frame); `ModuleGroundExpControl` scans only the parts loaded at that moment and does not set `DistanceToController` on the scan path (only the `onGroundSciencePartDeployed` path does).
- The three contracts' `Next(0, count - 1)` index never reaches the last candidate (`KSPRandom.Next(min, max)` is exclusive at the top).
- `DeployedScienceContract` / `ROCScienceArmContract` rewards differ from the defaults only through the WP-37 pipeline; the real `Generate` consumes Unity Random in `WeightedBodyChoice` before the agent is chosen, so a probe must make the same draw.

## Small fixes 2026-10-11 (wave 5, branch `wpfix5`, from main `7199d110`)

Seven items from the wave-3 / wave-4 gatekeepers; one commit each. `src/` changes are limited to item 2 and the cites of the two files it touches; everything else is tests, a script and notes.

1. **Linux vs Windows unit assertion gap (16): explained, a legitimate platform result, not a skipped test.** Per-case XML (`kspcore_tests -r=xml`) compared on MSVC and clang: exactly one case differs, `WP-03 vs KSP IL on .NET Framework 4.8` (11,032 vs 11,016 assertions). The 16 are the `Dbl()` helper of `CellEquals` (`tests/test_wp03_reference.cpp`, 2 `REQUIRE` per call, 2 calls per row), reached only when the recomputed double cell differs textually from the reference cell and both are NaN. The .NET reference NaN is the x86 "real indefinite" `0xFFF8000000000000`. MSVC produces `0x7FF8000000000000` for five rows (`UM ClampRadiansTwoPI`, `ClampDegrees360`, `ClampDegrees180`, `WrapAroundD` of +infinity, and `EVT DoubleMax`); on Linux the four `UM` rows are bit-equal to the reference (no fallback, no `Dbl()` call) and only `DoubleMax` still takes the fallback: 4 rows x 4 assertions = 16. The comparison is "NaN == NaN" by design (the comment above `CellEquals`), so both platforms assert the same property; the sign of a NaN is not observable by KSP code that does not look at the bits. No test is skipped and no data file is missing on Linux. Reproduce: `kspcore_tests -s -tc="WP-03 vs KSP IL*"` on both and count `SUCCESS` per source line (lines 64-65). The "Test results" `unit` row carries the note.
2. **`SqrtF` consolidated.** One `ksp::UnityNative::SqrtF` (`include/ksp/unity/quaternion_native.hpp`, beside the native quaternion functions; `Mathf::Sqrt` stays the Mono-float counterpart) replaces the file-local copies in `editor_gizmos.cpp`, `editor_logic.cpp` and `quaternion_native.cpp`. Same expression (`static_cast<float>(dotnet::Math::Sqrt(static_cast<double>(x)))`). Unit binary before / after (per-case doctest XML): identical assertion counts for every case that existed before, 0 failures.
3. **`tools/wp28/check_cites.py` exact mode.** Default: the cite line N must itself be a declaration line of the symbol (`candidates()`: the member name with its signature); a miss prints `<File>.cs:N -> K (name) off by k` and `--fix` rewrites N to the nearest declaration; `--window K` restores the legacy "name within +-K lines" check (the old behaviour is `--window 2`). ## Sanitizer run 2026-10-11 (branch `wpfix7`, from main `13750b33`)

Whole unit suite (`kspcore_tests`, 567 cases) under ASan + UBSan on WSL clang (`-fsanitize=address,undefined`, RelWithDebInfo, separate build dir). Result after the fixes: 567 cases / 935,279 assertions passed (Windows: 935,295, the known 16-assertion Linux difference), LeakSanitizer clean, ASan clean, one UBSan finding left in ported code.

Fixed (test-only unless noted):
- `tests/test_misc_modules.cpp` ModulePartFirework case: `tertiaryVisible` was a loop-body local captured by reference in the lambda installed in `FireworkEnvironment::setTertiaryColorVisible`; the next iteration's `OnStart` -> `configureColorFields` called the dangling lambda (stack-use-after-scope). Declared outside the loop.
- `src/dotnet/random.cpp` (ported code, behaviour unchanged): the seeding and sampling subtractions of `Random.cs` / `KSPRandom.cs` wrap in C# (unchecked); now computed in `uint32_t`. New case `tests/test_wp01_misc.cpp` "SystemRandom / KSPRandom seeding wrap-around": 9 seeds (INT32_MIN, INT32_MAX, negatives, 0, 1, 42, 1999999999), 8 draws each, expected values from an independent Python implementation with explicit 32-bit wrap (SystemRandom(42) first draw 1434747710 matches the well-known .NET value). All earlier WP-03 / KSPRandom assertions unchanged.
- `tools/support/craft_tree.hpp` `TestVessel` (the fixture behind `Part.vessel` in ~10 test files) was `reinterpret_cast` to `Vessel*`; `ModuleCargoBay` (`module_structural.cpp:132`, `:239`) reads `vessel->packed` / `->parts`, which is UB. `TestVessel` now owns a real bare `Vessel`; `handle()` returns it, `vesselHost` maps it back to the fixture through a registry, `Adopt` mirrors `parts`, the destructor clears the real vessel's parts before it dies.
- `tests/test_timing.cpp:527`: an intentionally leaked `std::vector<std::string>` log became a function-static.

Remaining finding in ported code (not fixed):
- (fixed 2026-10-12 by wpfix8, see "Sanitizer run 2026-10-12") `src/contracts/contract.cpp:399` and `:400` (`Contract::SetupID`, signed 64-bit overflow in `num = num * 23LL + ...`): the C# (`Contract.cs:1190` SetupID, unchecked `long` arithmetic) wraps. Fix would be to compute in `uint64_t`; results are already the wrapped values on all three compilers.

Tooling note: the full ASan+UBSan run takes about 3 hours here (build ~2 h on the shared WSL).

## Sanitizer run 2026-10-12 (branch `wpfix8`, from main `1f570809`)

Whole unit binary (`kspcore_tests`, 806 cases) under ASan + UBSan with g++ 13.3 on WSL (Ubuntu 24.04; clang is not installed there), RelWithDebInfo, separate build dir on the WSL ext4 filesystem, `testdata/` identical to the Windows tree. Result after the fixes: **one process, 806 cases, 1,326,275 assertions, 0 failed (Windows: 1,326,291, the known 16-assertion Linux difference), ASan clean, UBSan clean, LeakSanitizer clean (`detect_leaks=1`).** No suppression file.

Reproduce (from the repo root in WSL, after copying or cloning the worktree to the ext4 filesystem):

```bash
cmake -S core -B asan -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++ -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc   "-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -g"
CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=6 ninja -C asan -j6 kspcore_tests
cd asan/tests && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1 ./kspcore_tests          # whole binary, one process
# one process per case (a first ASan report aborts the process, so this lists every finding at once):
for i in $(seq 1 806); do ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ./kspcore_tests -f=$i -l=$i > run_$i.log 2>&1 || echo "case $i rc=$?"; done
```

Findings and fixes (the first sweep, one process per case, listed 36 failing cases; every number a gate checks is unchanged):
1. `Vessel::~Vessel` (`src/vessel/vessel.cpp`) read `p->vessel` of parts that tests (and any caller) had already destroyed (about 25 cases: test_fineprint2 / fineprint3 `VRig` / `SentinelRig`, test_inventory_deploy `EvaKerbal`, test_node_library `World`, test_construction_flow). Product fix: `~Vessel` only dereferences parts still registered in `Part::allParts` (a destroyed Unity object reads as null). wp19a (merged to main first) made the same fix at the top of `~Vessel` (it prunes `parts` and `rootPart` to the live set before `RemoveVessel`, and `FlightGlobals::RemoveVessel` removes every occurrence); on merging, wpfix8's own per-part `std::find` guard in the final loop was dropped as redundant, so `src/vessel/vessel.cpp` is identical to main and the other findings below are what wpfix8 adds. A first attempt that also made `Part::~Part` null its `vessel->parts` entry was dropped: WP-13 tests give `Part::vessel` an opaque fake pointer, which that destructor would dereference.
2. WP-33 `EVAConstructionModeEditor::OnDestroy` -> `RemoveAttachNodes` / `handleAttachNodeIcons` read the selected part and the attach vessels' parts after the test fixtures had freed them (test_construction.cpp x2 incl. the `Place / Move / Rotate` and `CheckAttach` cases, test_construction_flow.cpp x2, test_inventory_deploy.cpp `UpdatePartPlacementPosition`). Test-order fix: the editor/controller are declared after every part and vessel they point at (inventory_deploy: the three parts are declared before the editor and assigned later). No product change: the editor does not own the parts.
3. WP-53 `DeployedScience::~DeployedScience` -> `RemoveMannedScienceObjects` called `DestroyGameObject` on clusters already released by `SerenityBehaviour::FlushDestroyed` (test_serenity.cpp, the save/load case). Product fix, following `DeployedScience.cs:451` (only live children of the game object are destroyed): new `SerenityBehaviour::IsLive`, destroyed clusters are skipped.
4. WP-53 test_serenity.cpp seismic case (`d` was a reference into `seismicPartList`, whose data `ProcessSeismicEvent` frees three frames later): the test now takes a copy.
5. WP-38c `CompatibilityUtilities::UpdateCareerSave` (`src/fineprint/compatibility.cpp`): the `RecordTrackContract` branch removes the contract node from its list (the `shared_ptr` was the last owner) and the common `PARAM` pass below still reads it, as the C# does (the object lives on). Product fix: a local `shared_ptr` keeps the node alive for the loop body.
6. UBSan `Contract::SetupID` (`src/contracts/contract.cpp`): the unchecked `long` `num * 23 + hash` of `Contract.cs:1190` is now computed in `unsigned long long` (`wrapMulAdd23`); bit-identical results. `ContractParameter::CreateID` (`ContractParameter.cs:722`, same `* 23` pattern, no test reaches the overflow) got the same treatment.
7. UBSan `Waypoint::uniqueSeed` (`include/ksp/contracts/waypoints.hpp`, `Waypoint.cs:122`): `(index + seed) * (index + seed + 1) / 2 + seed` in 32-bit `int` wraps in C#; now computed in `uint32_t` (same value, the division is on the wrapped signed product). Hit by one WP-38 case (test_fineprint2.cpp:1124, five reports).
8. UBSan test_space_center.cpp:928 (the expected `prod / 2 + h` of the PQSCity seed check overflowed `int`): the sum is formed in `uint32_t`.

Not defects of the code, found while triaging: the earlier report that WP-14 / WP-16 / WP-18 ... exited non-zero with no ASan report in the wp19a WSL copy does not reproduce here: with the Windows tree's `testdata/` every one of those cases passes (the copy lacked data). Three cases are order dependent and fail when run alone with `-f=N -l=N` (the whole binary passes): #49 `WP-39 CommNetVessel: control state evaluation ...` (the `CommNetVessel` module class is registered by an earlier case; run alone `NewCommNetVessel` gets a plain `VesselModule`, a UBSan downcast report then a crash), #182 `WP-40 EditorLogic symmetry mode cycling` (needs the localization an earlier case loads), #425 `PartLoader on the GameData mirror` (360 instead of 362 parts alone). They are test-independence issues, not memory errors; left as they are.

Verification: Windows MSVC, `core/build` deleted, `run_tests.ps1 -Fresh` (`CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=6`): 35/35 ctest tests; `kspcore_tests` 806 cases, 1,326,291 assertions, 0 failed (identical to main `ea132145`: 806 / 1,326,291). WSL g++ ASan + UBSan + LSan: 806 cases, 1,326,275 assertions (Windows minus the known 16), no report.

### Findings (KSP behaviour kept as written)

- `ControlTypes` declares two members with value 0 (`None`, `STAGE_IN_MAP_CONTROLS`); Mono's flags `ToString` has no exact-name shortcut and always lists the second zero member first.
- `InputLockManager.SetControlLock` fires `onGUILock` (and the tooltip event) when the GUI bit was set before and is CLEAR afterwards; `RemoveControlLock` fires `onGUIUnlock` when it was clear before and is set afterwards: the names are inverted against the transition.
- `KeyCodeExtended(string)` parses with `Enum.Parse`: numbers become key codes (`160` in several shipped layouts is `KeyCode` 160, printed back as `160`), `W, A` ORs two names, anything unparsable keeps the text as a typed-character name.
- `KeyBinding.Load` keeps `group` / `modeMaskSec` when the node lacks them but resets `primary` / `secondary` to None; `AxisBinding_Single.Load` ends in `idTag = name` when the axis index is -1, so an unnamed binding is "NULL", not "None" (which would disable the axis).
- `GameSettings.WriteCfg` writes every public static field with `Convert.ToString`: `AXIS_INCREMENTAL_SPEED_MULTIPLIER_VALUES` goes out as `System.Collections.Generic.List`1[System.Single]` (and is never parsed), `ORBIT_WARP_MAXRATE_MODE` is written but not parsed back, floats use Mono's 7-digit "G" while `ConfigNode.AddValue(float)` (the binding fields) uses "G9" (`deadzone = 0.100000001`).
- A layout `dependency = Qwerty.cfg` resolves through the layouts loaded so far (file order: `Directory.GetFiles`); a dependency that is not loaded yet is read as a path relative to the working directory and silently yields an empty base.
- The first `FixedUpdate` with an unbound throttle axis (`AXIS_THROTTLE` None, neutral -1) jumps `throttle` to -1 (`|axis - lastAxisThrottle| > 0.25`) unless `refocusThrottle` was set (`SetLaunchCtrlState`, `OnApplicationFocus`, `ResumeVesselCtrlState`).
- `AxisKeyBinding.Clone` / `AxisKeyBindingList.Clone` are shallow: the copies share the three binding objects (a Load through the clone changes the original).

### Seams (documented; owner)

- `Mission.Load` in MISSION mode dereferences `situation.startingActionsNode`: a file with NODES but no SITUATION throws (NullReferenceException); `HighLogic.SaveFolder.Substring(SavesPath.Length)` throws for a short save folder.

- `#autoLOC_8100160` (Resource score description) uses `<<0>>..<<2>>`: the Localizer drops `<<0>>`, so the text shows min in slot 1 and max in slot 2 shifted by one (the reference reproduces it).
- `UpdateMission` calls `DoEndMissionActions` on every call while the active node is an end node (no `isEnded` test): score and awards would re-apply; MissionSystem must stop calling it.
- `AwardModule_Traveled*` and `AwardModule_Fuel` accumulate on every `EvaluateCondition` call (never reset).
- `TestModule.UpdateNodeBodyUI` dereferences `node.guiNode` without a null test (ActionModule guards it).
- `BuildReversePathsByDFS` returns an unregistered empty list for an orphan start node.

## WP-20a: physics world, frame model, Jolt vendored (branch `wp20a`, from `jolt-spike` head `b3b70db5`, PR #14; `origin/main` merged)

State: done for the engine-agnostic part. Scope = `core/PHYSICS-SPIKE.md` package WP-20a (section 7); vessel rigid bodies and joints (WP-20b / WP-20c) are not here.
**No golden or capture can cover it** (PhysX is a different solver and Jolt is not bit-reproducible against it), so the gate is analytic unit tests
(`tests/test_physics_world.cpp`, 14 cases / 147 assertions; no ctest test added, they run inside `unit`) and the Linux GCC build. Every existing gate is unchanged;
`harness/compare/tolerances.json` and `tests/tolerances_capture.json` untouched.

### What is in

| piece | files | KSP source it replaces / ports |
|---|---|---|
| Jolt v5.6.0 vendored | `third_party/jolt/{Jolt/,Build/CMakeLists.txt,LICENSE,README.md,SHA256SUMS}`, `cmake/ksp_jolt.cmake` | the spike's FetchContent (network) |
| `PhysicsWorld` | `include/ksp/physics/physics_world.hpp`, `src/physics/physics_world.cpp` (glue, RTTI-free), `physics_world_loop.cpp` (PlayerLoop hook) | the PhysX scene Unity stepped at FixedUpdate.PhysicsFixedUpdate; `Physics.gravity = 0` kept (gravity is a force); `CollisionManager.cs:126-168` as a `GroupFilter` |
| Krakensbane | `include/ksp/physics/krakensbane.hpp`, `src/physics/krakensbane.cpp` | `Krakensbane.cs:31-208` statement by statement; the shift consequence moved to `FloatingOrigin::FrameOffset()` |
| FloatingOrigin | `include/ksp/physics/floating_origin.hpp`, `src/physics/floating_origin.cpp` | `FloatingOrigin.cs:102-164, 166, 315-338` minus the world shift |
| Reference frame | `include/ksp/physics/reference_frame.hpp`, `src/physics/reference_frame.cpp` | `OrbitPhysicsManager.cs:234-304, 322-343` (decision + rotating-frame velocity re-expression), `FlightGlobals.cs:1356-1373` |

Frame model as implemented (PHYSICS-SPIKE.md 5.1): positions are doubles in the main body's frame, body-fixed below `inverseRotThresholdAltitude`, inertial above (KSP's own
`checkReferenceFrame` rule, unchanged); nothing is shifted per tick. A body's physics-frame velocity is its true velocity minus `Krakensbane::GetFrameVelocity()`
(`Vessel.cs` `velocityD = rb_velocityD + Krakensbane.GetFrameVelocity()`, read in the other direction), and its true position is the physics-frame position plus
`FloatingOrigin::FrameOffset()` = the sum of `FrameVel * fixedDeltaTime` over completed ticks (one double vector instead of the O(objects) shift of `setOffset`).
`ReferenceFrame::TrueVelocity / PhysicsVelocity / TruePosition / PhysicsPosition` do the conversions. The existing WP-20 seams (the `krakensbaneFrameVelocity` /
`krakensbaneAddFrameVelocity` hooks in `vessel.hpp`, `misc_modules.hpp`, `parachutes.hpp`, `FlightIntegratorAero::krakensbaneFrameVelocity`) are untouched; WP-19 wires them to `Krakensbane::GetFrameVelocity()`.

### Gate (all pass on MSVC RelWithDebInfo and on Linux GCC 13.3 Release)

| case | assertion | measured |
|---|---|---|
| double positions | a body at (600000.001, -3.5e-3, 12345678.125) reads back bit-exactly | exact |
| free fall, 5 s | equals the semi-implicit Euler solution `y0 - g dt^2 n(n+1)/2` to 5e-4 m, the continuous solution to `g dt t / 2` | within |
| box on a static floor | rests at y = 0.5 +- 0.05 (penetration slop 0.02), speed < 0.05 m/s, x / z undisturbed at 1e5 / 2e5 m | within |
| same-vessel filter | same group never collides; both `sameVesselCollision` collide; different group / ungrouped collide | 5 cases |
| determinism | 96-body pile (boxes, spheres, contacts), 200 steps: the `StateHash` (FNV-1a over the bits of every position, rotation, velocity) is identical twice and at 1, 2, 4, 8 threads, also at step 50 | identical |
| `Attach` | `PlayerLoop::Frame(.., 5)` steps the world 5 times; after `Detach` no more | exact |
| `SafeToEngage` | the 150 m / 50 m margins, 3000 m/s descent, landed, dead, two loaded vessels (altThreshold 200), other vessel low / landed (both flags) | all rules |
| frame velocity | AddExcess moves the whole velocity into `FrameVel`, events fire with the C# arguments, static bodies untouched, 501 ticks: physics-frame position bit-unchanged, `FrameOffset()` = `V dt n` (rel 1e-12), true velocity = 2000 exactly; landing disengages and returns the velocity | exact / 1e-12 |
| Kepler orbit, 1 revolution (r = 700 km, T = 1958.13 s, 97,906 ticks of 0.02 s, gravity at the true position) | radius error, end position error against the analytic circle | plain (no frame velocity): 23.7 m / 8.0 m; Krakensbane every tick: 22.5 m / 0.20 m; re-centred at 50 m/s: 22.5 m / 0.39 m with 283 instead of 97,906 velocity writes. The 22 m is the O(dt) offset of semi-implicit Euler (the spike measured 23 m); the frame velocity removes the float-velocity part of the end error |
| body-fixed frame orbit | a quarter orbit integrated in the rotating frame with `getCoriolisAcc` + `getCentrifugalAcc` against the inertial circle rotated back (Rodrigues about the rotation axis) | 42.6 m (the 22 m offset plus rotating-frame terms) |
| rotating frame switch | decision at, below, above the threshold, non-rotating body; `omega x r` re-expression of two bodies of a group and `krakensbaneAcc`, events, `FlightLogger.IgnoreGeeForces(0.5)` hook, there and back | 1e-6 rel (float velocity) |
| fictitious accelerations | `getCoriolisAcc`, `getCentrifugalAcc` against hand-derived values for omega = (0, -w, 0) | 1e-14 rel |

On Linux GCC the same numbers (plain end error 9.5 m instead of 8.0 m: a different binary) are inside the same bounds. Clang on Linux was not available locally (CI covers it).

### Build and CI impact

- Vendored Jolt: 5.6 MB source (561 files, `SHA256SUMS`, which lists the repository (LF) content). The `Jolt` static library compiles in about 43 s of CPU (132 objects, about 8 s wall at 6 jobs) against about 1,025 s of CPU for the rest of kspcore + tests (`.ninja_log`): roughly +4 % of a full build; incremental builds do not touch it.
- No network access: `FetchContent` is gone from the spike too (`spikes/jolt/CMakeLists.txt` now uses the vendored target).
- Link requirement: `kspcore.lib` now needs `Jolt.lib` / `libJolt.a` (`<build>/third_party/jolt/`) in the link line of every consumer built outside CMake (the Unreal bridge, `ue5/`: not touched here). CMake consumers get it through `$<LINK_ONLY:Jolt>`. Jolt needs an AVX2 CPU (its defaults).
- The glue `physics_world.cpp` is the only TU with Jolt's flags; it is built without RTTI like Jolt (GCC / Clang fail to link otherwise: `typeinfo for JPH::GroupFilter`), so the PlayerLoop hook (the `Delegate` uses `typeid`) is in `physics_world_loop.cpp`.
- Jolt warnings never fail the build (`ENABLE_ALL_WARNINGS=OFF`, glue `/wd4100 /wd4324 /wd4127 /external:W0`, GCC `-Wno-class-memaccess -Wno-psabi`); the new files add no warnings of their own on MSVC or GCC.

### Deviations and decisions (all documented in the headers)

1. **No world shift**: `FloatingOrigin` keeps its API and fields, never applies `setOffset` to bodies / vessels / particles; `Offset()` is a one-tick value the host may set with `SetOffset`, and `onFloatingOriginShift` is not fired. `TerrainShaderOffset`, `CollisionEnhancer.bypass`, the threshold / continuous / `bypassAuto` decision are dropped.
2. **Krakensbane without instance**: the C# throws `NullReferenceException` (`fetch` is null); the static readers return zero here.
3. **`Krakensbane::recentreSpeed`** (kspcore addition, default 0 = KSP's rule: the whole rb velocity moves into `FrameVel` every tick while the vessel is faster than 5 m/s). With 50 m/s the frame velocity is only re-centred above that physics-frame speed (PHYSICS-SPIKE.md): 283 writes instead of 97,906 per orbit for the same orbit.
4. **Ordering constraint for WP-19a**: gravity must read the true position before `FloatingOrigin::FixedUpdate` consumes this tick's out-of-frame offset (equivalently the offset is consumed after the step). Consuming it before evaluating gravity put the force one `FrameVel * dt` (45 m) ahead of the body and produced a 565 m radius error in the first test run; the tests document the order.
5. **Jolt body defaults** (`BodyDesc`): no damping (KSP applies its own drag), no sleeping, `maxLinearVelocity` 1e5 (Jolt's default 500 m/s cap destroys any orbit: found by the orbit test), `maxAngularVelocity` 50 (Physics.cfg).
6. **Determinism flags**: the spike's configuration (`CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC` OFF: deterministic for one binary and call order, independent of the thread count, not across compilers / OSes). Hashes are compared inside a process only; nothing stores a literal. `-DKSP_JOLT_DETERMINISTIC=ON` builds the cross-platform mode (not gated).
7. **No std:: maths in ported code**: `krakensbane.cpp`, `floating_origin.cpp`, `reference_frame.cpp` use only Vector3d arithmetic (all `double`, as the C#); there is no float32 statement in the ported functions, so the Mono float rule has nothing to apply to. The glue and the tests use std maths (not ported KSP code). `check_cites.py` exact mode (`--cs-root` Assembly-CSharp) over the three ported `.cpp` files: 15 citations, 0 mismatches.

| vessel rigid bodies, part / cluster build, `AddForceAtPosition` per part, mass updates, `Flush` | WP-20b |

### Quirks reproduced / found (a later implementer must keep them)

- `VesselPrecalculate` runs for EVERY vessel (loaded or not) before the OrbitDriver; `MainPhysics` sets `orbitDriver.QueueOnce` so `OrbitDriver.FixedUpdate` does not update
  the orbit a second time. A vessel destroyed by `CheckKill` earlier in the same frame is skipped by `FlightScene`.
- The orbit drift compensation works against the orbit refit from the same state in the previous `Update` (`TrackRigidbody(..., -fdtLast)`): it makes the Euler step
  land on the Kepler step from the CURRENT state each tick (pre-integration velocity offset), and corrects the velocity after the step (post-integration correction,
  applied in the next MainPhysics or in `Update`). It does nothing in an atmosphere (`altitude > atmosphereDepth`, `staticPressurekPa == 0`) or above
  `OrbitDriftAltThreshold`. The first tick after creation runs the packed-style stats branch, so compensation starts on the second tick.
- `DOCKED` appears only in `VesselRanges` masks and contract checks; `updateSituation` never sets it. PRELAUNCH -> LANDED needs `srfSpeed > 2.5` and no easing / spawning.
- `OrbitPhysicsManager.Start` is a coroutine polling every 0.5 s; here `Start()` is polled by the caller (no 0.5 s granularity).
- `OrbitPhysicsManager.setDominantBody` fires `onDominantBodyChange(dominantBody, body)` AFTER assigning, so both arguments are the new body.
- `Vessel.CheckKill` second block (`crashed through terrain`) uses `terrainAltitude`, which is -1 for an unloaded vessel without a PQS: the limit is then -0.1 m (-250 m loaded).
- `FlightGlobals.getHomeBody` / `getBodyByName` caches in the C# survive nothing but the scene; kspcore validates a cached body against `Bodies()`.

- WP-19b: `setRotatingFrame` / `setDominantBody` effects, `ChangeWorldVelocity`, rebase on vessel switch, multiple loaded vessels (`two_vessels`), `physicalObjects`.
- WP-20b: everything behind `readPhysicsState`, `offsetVelocity`, `rootRigidbody`, `packPart` ... (the VesselPhysics object per loaded unpacked vessel).
- `QuickSaveLoad` / `VesselRetrieval` (UI and file orchestration); the debug orbit setters; the navball orientation of `UpdateInformation`.
- A new in-game capture of `VesselPrecalculate` in / out per tick (pad, ascent, orbit: gAccel, integrationAccel, coriolis, centrifugal, pre / post offsets) would turn the
  loaded-vessel formulas into a capture gate; today they are gated against the independent Python reference, and `world_rel` needs the game's absolute body positions.

### wp19a ASan finding (Linux CI SIGSEGV in "WP-55 reference: Actions.*")

Root cause (reproduced with g++ `-fsanitize=address,undefined`, WSL): `~Vessel` (Vessel.OnDestroy) reads its `parts` and `protoVessel` (WP-14: the `p->vessel == this` loop; WP-19a: `FlightGlobals.RemoveVessel` also reads the parts' persistent ids), and the WP-55 test `World` freed its parts and proto vessels BEFORE its vessels (member order), a use-after-free that was benign on a lucky heap and became a SIGSEGV once the registry read more of it. Fixes: (1) `tests/test_node_library.cpp`: `World` declares `vessels` last (destroyed first) [WP-55 test]; (2) product: `~Vessel` drops parts that are no longer in `Part::allParts` (a destroyed Unity Part is `null` in the C# lists) and `rootPart` likewise before touching them; (3) product: `FlightGlobals::RemoveVessel` removes every occurrence from all three lists (a vessel registered twice, as `test_serenity.cpp`'s `Mk` does after `Initialize`, or whose `loaded` flag changed without SortVessel, left a dangling pointer that `RefreshViews` then read). With these the WP-55, WP-19a, WP-39 CommNetVessel, WP-20a ASan runs are clean. Still reported by ASan, all outside wp19a and unchanged by it: test-side destruction order in `test_construction.cpp` / `test_construction_flow.cpp` (EVAConstructionModeEditor OnDestroy reads freed parts), `test_serenity.cpp` (DeployedScience destructor), and `CompatibilityUtilities::UpdateCareerSave` (`fineprint/compatibility.cpp:193` reads a freed ConfigNode list); UBSan reports intentional signed-overflow hashing in `contracts/contract.cpp:399-400`. (All of these were fixed afterwards by wpfix8, see "Sanitizer run 2026-10-12".)

Follow-up (PR #21 CI, g++ only): `unit.random_order.11` crashed with SIGSEGV in `WP-33 ModuleInventoryPart.OnUpdate: container highlight decision in flight`. Cause: `EVAConstructionModeController::hooks` is a static; `test_inventory_ui.cpp` assigns `hooks.evaEnterExitConstruction` to a lambda capturing its stack locals and never clears it, so the next case that opens the construction panel called a dangling lambda (ASan: stack-use-after-return at test_inventory_ui.cpp:341). `std::shuffle` differs between libstdc++ and MSVC, so the seed gives another order per platform and the pair only met under g++. Fix: `Reset33::Clear()` and the hygiene listener reset `hooks`. Reproduced in WSL by building the PR's CI commit; ASan + UBSan clean for seeds 11, 27, 42 afterwards.

### Measurements (Release, pinned, best of 3; `spikes/jolt/results/wp20b_regression.md`)

Tick time of the full scenario (per-part pipeline + binding + Jolt), one thread: S 0.017 ms, M2-AS 0.113, L2-AS 0.340, XL1-AS 0.793, XL2-AS
1.617 (the spike's reduced-whole in the same session: 0.017, 0.105, 0.312, 0.854, 1.484). The binding's own share at 457 parts: ReadState
0.028 ms (KSP's full CalculatePhysicsStats incl. its MOI loop, which the spike skipped), Flush 0.002, Jolt step 0.003, AfterStep (pose cache +
transform sync) 0.010. The bit-identical diagonal-only MOI loop costs 0.021 ms at 457 parts (the 4 x 4 form: 0.036). XL1-AS / XL2-AS
trajectories with the spike's damping: +0.005 % / +0.02 % and +0.002 % / +0.001 % of the spike's.

### Exact / approximate / changed, per choice

| choice | class | notes |
|---|---|---|
| which parts have a Rigidbody (Part.Start), physicsless parts riding on RigidBodyPart, their mass folded in by UpdateMassStats | exact | the C# rules |
| one body per cluster of welded parts (every attach joint except articulation points) | changed (decided) | no joint compliance, no wobble; trajectories vs the articulated model within 0.5 % (above) |
| rb.mass = Max(partInfo.MinimumRBMass, physicsMass) | exact | the spike used PhysicsGlobals.PartRBMassMin |
| rb.inertiaTensor = per-unit tensor x Max(1, rb.mass), rotation identity | rule exact, tensor approximate | the per-unit tensor is the solid box of the first drag cube (proxy collider, R6), not PhysX's tensor of the .mu colliders |
| cluster mass / CoM / inertia | exact sums | KSP's loop order (last part first); bit-identical to WP-14 where rb.mass == physicsMass; double |
| physicsless parts' colliders in their parent's compound | exact | Unity: the colliders of a child GameObject belong to the parent's Rigidbody |
| ReadState = CalculatePhysicsStats over the clusters | exact formulas, double frame | bit-identical to the float path at rest; positions are doubles (KSP: floats near the floating origin) |
| forces at their points (Part.AddForce at RigidBodyPart's CoM, AddForceAtPosition, AddTorque, ForceMode), summed to force + torque about the cluster CoM | exact | the rigid-body equivalent of the per-part forces of a welded assembly |
| FlightIntegrator.Integrate force half | exact order | incl. the dropped buffers of physicsless parts |
| angular drag `PerPart` (default) | approximate | removes sum_i (1 - max(0, 1 - dt d_i)) I_i w per step (I_i the part's own tensor) as a torque: PhysX's per-body damping of a rigid assembly to first order in dt; the orbital part m r x v is not damped, as in KSP |
| angular drag `ClusterMassAverage` | changed (the spike's) | kept to reproduce the spike; damps the whole I_c w |
| rb.angularDrag before FlightIntegrator sets it: 0.05 | exact | Unity's Rigidbody default |
| mass change: the CoM moves inside the body, velocity v + w x shift | exact | the parts keep their velocities |
| Part.ResumeVelocity at the cluster CoM | approximate | KSP sets each part to V - w_body x r_part (a rigid rotation the joints sort out); the cluster gets the mass-weighted mean exactly, angular velocity unchanged |
| bodies destroyed on rails (packPart), rebuilt on unpack | changed | KSP keeps kinematic bodies; nothing in gameplay needs a packed vessel's bodies (PHYSICS-SPIKE.md 5.4) |
| same-vessel collision of clusters | exact for single-part clusters, approximate otherwise | a cluster collides with its vessel's other clusters only if all its parts have sameVesselCollision (Jolt filters per body, KSP per collider pair) |
| PartJoint data | exact rules (Mono float rule), anchors / axes approximate | the Transform maths goes through PartTransform (Unity's native matrix rounding not reproduced); autostrut Heaviest is the spike's rule (heaviest rb.mass), GetMassivePart's tree walk with its per-tick cache is WP-20c's |
| inter-cluster joints: one fixed weld per cluster pair | changed | WP-20c (compliant / breakable) and WP-52 (motors) replace it |
| Cut / SplitOff / Merge / Rebuild | exact conservation | every new cluster takes the linear and angular momentum of its parts |
| friction 0.6, restitution 0 | approximate | Unity's default PhysicMaterial; KSP's part collider materials are not extracted |
| no gyroscopic torque | exact (as PhysX in Unity) | a tumbling body keeps w, not L |
| frames (physics-frame doubles, world = frameOriginWorld + TruePosition, the transform frame for the float fields) | exact (WP-20a's model) | see the header of `vessel_physics.hpp` |

| seam | owner |
|---|---|
| the load solve over `PartExternalForces / Moments` and the cluster accelerations, capacity per `PartJointSpec`, breaking via `Cut`; wiring `Cut` / `OnVesselSplit` / `OnVesselMerge` into Part.decouple / Undock / Couple / joint breaks (GameEvents); autostrut rebuild on vessel change; Heaviest anchors | WP-20c |

### Risks

- R1 (the frame of the float fields): with `floatOrigin` != 0 (a vessel-local float frame, the spike's choice) `Vessel.CoM = CoMD.ToVector3f()` and
  `localCoM = vesselTransform.InverseTransformPoint(CoM)` mix frames in CalculatePhysicsStats (WP-19a code); with 0 (KSP's convention) the world
  must be near the vessel. WP-19b decides (the floating origin of the render / bubble).
- R2 (contact solver limit cycles): a vessel standing on many contacts can keep rocking at a few cm/s depending on Jolt's body order (M2-AS: exact
  rest on the spike's 30 x 30 terrain patch, 7 cm/s on a 4 x 4 patch). WP-20e's landed anchor (a still landed cluster made kinematic,
  PHYSICS-SPIKE.md R7) removes it in play.
- R3 (float velocities): an orbiting vessel without Krakensbane's frame velocity drifts metres per orbit (measured 5.2 m); hosts must run
  Krakensbane in orbit (KSP does).
- R4: Windows vs Linux bit-identity is not measured (PHYSICS-SPIKE.md R8); the tests compare inside one process only.
- R5: the proxy colliders (the spike's R6) shape both the contacts and the inertia tensors.

WP-29b (ModuleWheelBase, ModuleWheels/*) and WP-29c (the native WheelCollider / suspension law) are not part of this package.

### Ported (`include/ksp/wheels/`, `src/wheels/`; every function carries a `File.cs:line` cite, `tools/wp28/check_cites.py` and `tools/wp55/check_cites.py` exact mode: 215 cites, 0 mismatches)
- `tire_friction.cpp`: `TireFriction` (the five curves `Flat`, `Lineal`, `Smooth`, `Parametric`, `Pacejka` with their `Settings` / `ApplyAPLConstraints`, `GetForce`, `IsAdherentSlip`, the adherent slip / force helpers, the slip bounds), `MathUtility` (FastAbs, Vector3Equals, UnclampedLerp), `InterpolatedFloat`.

- `vehicle_base.cpp`: `VehicleBase` (the whole `FixedUpdate` pipeline: vehicle speed / local acceleration, suspension travel and forces, downforce with the contact-angle cosine and `minimumdownForce`, the local frame with the slope and impulse terms, the tyre force smoothing and application at the hit point with the dynamic-surface reaction, wheel sleep, `Update`, behaviours, pause / single step, state vars, impacts `OnCollision` / `ProcessImpacts` / `UpdateDragState`, the component lifecycle `enabled` -> `OnEnable` / `OnDisable`).

### Gate (`tests/test_wheels.cpp`, 12 cases / 7,513 assertions; ctest `wheels.vpp` runs the 12 `WP-29a*` cases; also part of `unit` and of the random-order runs)
- Reference: `tools/wp29a/vpp_reference.py` -> `tests/data/wp29a_reference.json` (7.4 MB, deterministic, seed 2902; regenerate with `python -I tools/wp29a/vpp_reference.py > tests/data/wp29a_reference.json`).
- How circularity was avoided: the Python was written first, from the C# text only (a different structure from the C++: numpy float32 / double helpers, tuple vectors, scripted scenes), before any C++ of this package existed; the C++ was then written from the C# again, never from the Python (one reference bug, an input that skipped its float store, was found by the gate and fixed on the Python side). Both transcribe the same C# statements, so they agree only where both transcribe correctly; the reference asserts that every value it emits is float32-exact (this caught one input that skipped the float store while it was being written). Independent mutation check: dropping a single `f32store` in `SmoothFriction::CubicLerp` fails the friction and wheel-chain gates at 1 ULP; replacing the RK4 sixth by its decimal truncation fails the wheel-chain gate at 3 ULP (restored).
- Sweeps: (1) tyre curves: 5 settings sets (defaults, the stock-like three-point curve, constraint-violating values for `ApplyAPLConstraints` and the Pacejka clamps) x 5 models x 60 slip vectors (at / around adherent, peak and limit slip, below 1e-6, axis aligned, random) x load {0 .. 133.7} x grip x frictionMultiplier: 1,500 rows, 16,500 values. (2) the wheel / DirectDrive / Solver chain driven directly: 90 scenarios, 10,800 ticks, 226,890 values: radius 0.1 .. 1.0 m, mass 0.01 .. 100 t (61 scenarios sit on the 0.01 t m^2 inertia floor), dt 0.005 / 0.02 / 0.04 / 0.1, Euler with 1 / 4 / 8 substeps and RK4 (22 scenarios), Smooth and Lineal curves, load 0 .. 40, slip velocities -15 .. 25 m/s, external forces, motor ramps and rpm limits, 2,895 ticks with the 1000 kN m locking brake. (3) the whole `FixedUpdate` + `Update` pipeline over 24 scripted scenes (12 families x 2: flat drive, airborne transitions, slopes, moving dynamic and kinematic surfaces, landing-leg lock with `minimumdownForce = 10`, steering, ground materials, reference-frame fix off, RK4 / substeps, the inertia floor, Lineal rebuilt, Lineal NOT rebuilt), 3,600 ticks (3,381 grounded, 219 airborne), 349,200 values per run: every `WheelState` field, the wheel block state, the vehicle speed, every native write (centre, suspension distance, radius, spring, damper, target position, force application point, steer angle, motor torque), the hit after the fix-ups, the force calls on the wheel body and on the surface body. All 0 ULP.
- Smooth versus Lineal: both curves are gated in (1), (2) and (3). **UNVERIFIED pending capture C11**: `ModuleWheelBase.cs:361` assigns `tireFriction.model = Lineal` after the controller's `TireFriction` has built its `SmoothFriction` and nothing rebuilds the curve (`SetupFrictionCurves` runs only from the constructor and `OnAfterDeserialize`), so a stock wheel runs the Smooth curve over settings the module mutates in place. The port keeps that (family `lineal_not_rebuilt`; case "the Lineal-never-rebuilt quirk"); whether the game really behaves so needs the C11 capture (WHEEL-SPIKE.md Q1).
- Derived cases (from the C# control flow, labelled in the file): lifecycle and error paths (Awake in a game scene, Initialize then `enabled = true`, "Missing WheelCollider", "Invalid wheel properties", missing rigidbody), brake ramp and the 1000 kN m rest brake, keyboard modes, steering ramp, properties, pause / single step, state vars, gravity cache (approximate `==`), impacts and callbacks, `GetGroundHit` when disabled, `ApplyForce` to dynamic and kinematic surface bodies, the advanced suspension damper (dead code: it dereferences the static `VehicleBase.vehicle`, which is null outside the impact callbacks, so it throws `NullReferenceException`).

### Natives (UNVERIFIED, no C# source exists)
`Transform.up / forward / right / InverseTransformPoint / InverseTransformDirection` (Unity `RotateVectorByQuat`, scale 1), `Rigidbody.GetPointVelocity` (PhysX `v + w x (p - com)`), float32 per operation in both implementations; `Quaternion.AngleAxis` in production is the capture-verified `UnityNative::AngleAxis` (UCRT `sinf` / `cosf`), which an independent Python cannot reproduce bit for bit: the pipeline gate rebinds the `NativeOps::AngleAxis` hook to the reference's formulation (`cos` / `sin` of the half angle from the correctly rounded double) and a separate case bounds the difference of the two bindings over 3 axes x 487 angles at 2 ULP. A capture of Transform.up / InverseTransformPoint and Rigidbody.GetPointVelocity would settle the first group.

### Findings kept from the C#
- `VehicleBase.CalculateSuspensionForces` (advanced damper) uses the STATIC `vehicle`, never assigned outside the impact callbacks: NullReferenceException (dead: KSP never sets `advancedSuspensionDamper`).
- `KSPWheelController.Initialize()` runs `OnInitialize`; `wheel.enabled = true` then runs `VehicleBase.OnEnable`, which calls `OnInitialize` AGAIN (fresh `Wheel` / `DirectDrive`, the controller's own `TireFriction` is kept) and primes the solver with one `Integrate(0, fixedDeltaTime, 1)`.
- `Wheel.Initialize` news a `TireFriction` that `OnInitialize` immediately replaces.
- `VehicleBase.FixedUpdate` uses `Time.deltaTime` as its step: under physics warp the tyre smoothing (`lerp(last, new, sharpness dt)`) and the impulse term scale with dt (WHEEL-SPIKE Q9).
- `GetSolverState` can loop forever on an unconnected input (not ported, diagnostics).

### Not ported
Unreachable from KSP (~20k lines): Engine, Gearbox, Driveline, Differential*, Clutch, Retarder, Brakes, Steering, Inertia, InertialFlywheel / Drive, VPVehicleController, VPVehicleJoint, VPAudio, VPDamage, VPTelemetry, DataLogger, DataRecorder, the charts, cameras, cargo, VPTireEffects, VPGroundMarksRenderer, VPGroundParticleEmitter, VPGroundMaterialManager, VPAntiRollBar, VPDynamicSuspension, VPRollingFriction, StabilityControl, EdyCommonTools TextureCanvas / GColor / MiniJSON / UdpConnection / CsvFile / Spline / CircularBuffer / camera and input helpers. Inside the ported files: `VehicleBase.GetSolverState` / `GetSolverBlockTypes`, `Disable / EnableCollidersRaycast`, the `Debug.DrawLine` gizmos, `VPWheelCollider.AdjustToWheelMesh` / `GetScaledBounds` / `OnValidate` / `OnDrawGizmosSelected`, the Transform writes of `UpdateVisualWheel` and the `wheelTransform` / `caliperTransform` / `suspensionTransform` fields with the `m_angularPosition` seed from `wheelTransform.localEulerAngles.x` (suspension / caliper / wheel mesh placement: the renderer's), `Solver.GetViscousLockingDt` (clutches / differentials), `Block.Connect(params)` and the 3-argument overloads. Root `Wheel.cs` (TestVehicleController only) and `ModuleWheels/WheelFrictionNode.cs` were never in scope.

### Residual risks
- The native seam formulas above, the Unity `WheelCollider` defaults (mass 20, radius 0.5, suspension distance 0.3, spring 35000 / 4500, target 0.5, only visible on the first tick) and the layer of `sprungMass` (WP-29c supplies it) are unverified.
- Scenes are open loop (scripted rigid-body and hit state): the closed-loop behaviour (spring, jounce, reaction on the body) belongs to WP-29c; the 1-D drive reference of WHEEL-SPIKE section 7 ("within 1 %") needs the module layer and is not part of this gate.
- Transcendentals (`Atan2`, `Cos`, `Acos`, `Sin`, `Atan`) go through `dotnet::Math` (the lifted VS2013 CRT); the Python uses the host libm and rounds to float32: they agree on every value of the gate, but a 1 ULP double difference landing on a float rounding boundary would show as a 1 ULP mismatch.

### Runs
Windows (MSVC, RelWithDebInfo): `kspcore_tests` 822 cases / 1,374,044 assertions pass in default order and with `--order-by=rand -rs=11` and `-rs=27`. g++ 13 ASan + UBSan + LSan (WSL, README "Sanitizer run"): no sanitizer report, no warning in `src/wheels`; the 22 failing cases of that run are craft-file / game-data cases (`test_vessel`, `test_staging`, `test_ship_construct`, `test_timewarp`) that need `harness/inputs` / `decompiled/KSP-dev` which the WSL copy did not include (not related to this package; all 12 `WP-29a` cases pass there).


## WP-12b: terrain colliders (branch `wp12b`, from main `b9119103`, main `a883a8ca` merged)

State: done for the engine-agnostic part. The WP-12a seam (`PQS::onQuadColliderEnabled / onQuadColliderDisabled`, fired by `PQSMod_QuadMeshColliders`) now builds and tears down static collision geometry in `PhysicsWorld`; PQSCity / PQSCity2 object colliders are ported as activation structures with fixture colliders; the terrain query API (ray cast down, height above terrain, surface normal, overlap) exists. Gated by an independent Python reference of the activation decisions (exact), analytic ray / normal checks, the measured agreement with WP-11 and a box dropped on the KSC pad. No KSP golden or capture can cover Jolt contacts (PhysX is not reproducible); `harness/compare/tolerances.json` and `tests/tolerances_capture.json` untouched, every earlier gate unchanged.

### What KSP decides (all from the C#, nothing assumed)

| fact | source |
|---|---|
| The whole activation rule: `minLevel = sphere.maxLevel - |maxLevelOffset|`; `OnQuadBuilt`: a quad with `subdivision >= minLevel` gets a `MeshCollider` (added once, stays on the pooled quad), enabled, `sharedMesh = quad.mesh`, `sharedMaterial = physicsMaterial`; `OnQuadDestroy`: disabled, mesh and material cleared. **There is no distance test anywhere in the collider mods**: which quads exist at the maximum levels is the quadtree's decision (WP-12a: target-driven subdivision), a collider appears when its quad is built and disappears when `PQS.DestroyQuad` runs | `PQSMod_QuadMeshColliders.cs:17-44`, `PQS.cs:1031`, `PQS.cs:2287`, `PQSCache.cs:448` |
| All 15 stock bodies have `maxLevelOffset = 0`: colliders exist on the built maximum-level quads only (Kerbin / Eve / Duna / Laythe / Tylo / Eeloo 10, Mun / Moho / Dres 8, ...; the default terrain preset caps Kerbin at 9: vertex spacing 154-157 m, Mun at 8: 100-101 m). A quad that becomes invisible or is subdivided KEEPS its collider until it is destroyed (SetInvisible / Subdivide never touch it) | `data/terrain/pqs_prefab.json`, `PQ.cs:802`, `PQSCache.cs:448` |
| Unity bakes the MeshCollider at the `sharedMesh` assignment: later `mesh.triangles` changes (edge-state stitching sets) do not reach the baked collider, so the collision triangles are `cacheIndices[0]` | `PQS.cs:2283`, `PQ.cs:294` |
| Layer: quads take the PQS GameObject's layer (15 "Local Scenery" is terrain and scatter, mask 32768 is what `PQSCity2.OrientateRayCast` casts against); KSP makes no `Physics.IgnoreLayerCollision` call | `PQS.cs:1015`, `PQSCity2.cs:354`, `analysis/physics/PHYSICS-ENGINE-REVIEW.md` section 7 |
| `PQS_Collider`, `PQS_ColliderAdvanced`, `PQS_PartCollider` are never instantiated by shipped code (only `Part.cs` destroys a `terrainCollider` that nothing creates); `PQSMod_CreateSphereCollider` is on no stock prefab; `PQSMod_SurfaceObjectQuads` / `SurfaceObject` re-parent vessels to quads for the floating origin (no collision) | grep of Assembly-CSharp, `pqs_prefab.json` |
| PQSCity colliders are the city's prefab children, switched by `transformsActive` (children active while the sphere has a target and is alive) and by `LODRange.objects` (sorted by `visibleRange`; active iff the float target distance is below the range); PQSCity2 by `LodObject` (active iff the squared distance is below `visibleRange^2`, `KeepActive` forces on, Setup / SetInactive switch everything off) | `PQSCity.cs:22-60, 168-260`, `PQSCity2.cs:10-60, 367-513` |

### The agreement bound with WP-11 (measured; Kerbin = scenario kerbin_ksc, Mun = scenario mun)

The collider is the PQS quad mesh: 15 x 15 vertices, 14 x 14 cells of 2 triangles, linear in between. Vertex spacing is 154-157 m (Kerbin, level 9) and 100-101 m (Mun, level 8). The vertices ARE WP-11's heights (WP-12a gate); the ray cast (`SurfaceAt`, radial line, from 400 m above) is compared with `GetSurfaceHeight` of an independent sphere in the build state of the quad (`Mod_OnQuadPreBuild` as in the WP-12a vertex gate):

| | Kerbin (72 quads) | Mun (16 quads) |
|---|---|---|
| rays through the 225 vertices of every quad | 16,192 of 16,200 hit; max abs difference **0.81 mm** (the 8 misses are exact rays through outermost border vertices of the collider region) | 3,595 of 3,600; max **1.6 mm** |
| 5 interior points per cell (70,560 / 15,680 rays, 0 misses) | max 39.8 m, mean 1.77 m, p99 8.54 m. By distance from the pad: < 200 m (27 samples) max **1.51 m**, mean 0.20 m; < 500 m (156) max 1.85 m, mean 0.38 m; < 1 km (627) max 4.74 m, mean 0.46 m; < 3 km (5,596) max 13.4 m, mean 1.02 m. The 6 worst samples (30-40 m) are 7-9 km from the pad in cells whose own corner relief is 32-87 m | max 31.4 m, mean 1.84 m, p99 14.7 m (rough crater terrain 5-6 km from the track) |
| max error / cell relief (corner radii max - min, cells > 1 m) | 2.7 | 1.9 |

So: **at the vertices the collider equals WP-11 to 2 mm; between vertices it differs by the terrain's own sub-cell relief, which is not bounded by the mesh alone (up to 2.7x the relief of the cell's corners); stated bounds: 1.5 m within 200 m of the KSC pad (0.32 m under the pad box), 40 m worst case over the 72 Kerbin collider quads, 31 m on the Mun.** This is a property of KSP's own collision surface (the same 15 x 15 maximum-level quad meshes), not of this port. The flat-sphere gate shows the machinery itself is exact: 0.3 mm against the analytic facet.

### Performance (Ryzen 9 7950X3D, `build/RelWithDebInfo/tests/wp12_bench.exe 3`, not pinned: the numbers vary +-20 % run to run)

| | Kerbin (KSC pad, 72 colliders) | Mun (16) |
|---|---|---|
| collider build per quad (snapshot + Jolt `MeshShape` cook + insert), first cook of every quad | **83 us** (mean of 216 cooks 86 us, median 78, max 159) | 79 us (mean 78, max 85) |
| all colliders of a scene load | 6.0 ms for 72 quads | 1.3 ms for 16 |
| `SurfaceAt` ray cast against the colliders (2000 queries) | 2.5 us | 2.6 us |
| for comparison: quad build (WP-12a) | 0.89 ms per quad (heights 0.87) | 1.1 ms |

The collider cook is about 8-10 % of the cost of building the quad it belongs to and 0.08 ms per quad: KSP's frame-time budget for building quads (PQS `maxFrameTime`) is dominated by the height stack, so the synchronous default adds no hitch worth budgeting; `maxCooksPerUpdate` exists for hosts that stream (a budget of 8 per Update is about 0.7 ms). Static bodies are not simulated: the colliders add no per-step cost beyond the broad phase.

Quads next to a lower-level neighbour have no collider on that neighbour's side (no collider below the maximum level) |
| 8 | PQSCity distance rules | changed (precision) | KSP: float world-space distances under the floating origin; port: double physics-frame distance narrowed to float for the comparison. Differs only within a float ulp of a `visibleRange` |

### Quirks reproduced / found

1. A quad that is subdivided or goes invisible keeps its collider (it is only disabled by `DestroyQuad`); with `maxLevelOffset = 0` this never overlaps anything, with an offset > 0 the parent's collider lies under its children's (synth_a, offset 1: 243 colliders at the end).
2. `OnQuadDestroy` fires the disable for every destroy of a quad that ever had a collider: repeated disables of a disabled collider are events (264 disables in synth_a).
3. A re-built quad's `OnQuadBuilt` re-assigns `sharedMesh`: the collider is replaced.
4. PQSCity `children` and `LODRange.objects` can name the same GameObject; the `transformsActive` toggle re-activates it regardless of `LODRange.isActive`, which does not see the change (tested).
5. `PQSCity2.LodObject.Setup` leaves `isActive = false` and `SetInactive` re-enables `KeepActive` objects.
6. Jolt's `CollideShape` takes the shape's WORLD transform; `baseOffset` only moves the origin of the returned contacts (found by `OverlapSphere` returning nothing).
7. The angle between two nearly parallel unit normals via `acos(dot)` is wrong by 4.5e-4 rad for a norm error of 1e-7: the tests use the chord `|n1 - n2|`.

2. KSC / airfield / launch-site scenery colliders (the `KSC.prefab` children, `LODRange` / `LodObject` objects with their BoxCollider / MeshCollider components and the .mu / Unity meshes of the buildings): level-scene and asset-bundle data, not extracted; `CityCollider` takes them as data, tests use labelled box fixtures. `PQSCity2.OrientateRayCast` (mobile launch pad) can now be given `TerrainColliders::RayDown`-style queries; wiring it is WP-42 / WP-47.

Wiring: who owns the `TerrainColliders` per body and sets `origin` / the target (WP-19b / WP-20d: the dominant body's sphere, `FlightGlobals.ActiveVessel` as `PQSTarget`; above `inverseRotThresholdAltitude` the physics frame is inertial and terrain colliders must not be used there: PHYSICS-SPIKE 5.5).
4. The general `RayCast` / `LineCast` users (Vessel ground height `Vessel.cs:2493-2712`, `CollisionEnhancer`, engine exhaust damage, wheel suspension) are WP-20d / WP-29: they call `PhysicsWorld::RayCast`; `TerrainColliders::HeightAboveTerrain` is the terrain-only variant.
5. The C ABI does not expose colliders (the UE shell renders; Chaos / Jolt choice for UE-side collision is the shell's).
6. Ocean child spheres (no colliders in KSP either: the water is `PartBuoyancy`, WP-20e).

## WP-20c: the structural layer of the reduced rigid-body model (branch `wp20c`, from local `wp20b` `950c1d94`; merged)

State: done for the engine-agnostic part. Scope = `core/PHYSICS-SPIKE.md` section 7 row WP-20c and the WP-20b seams list ("the load solve over
`PartExternalForces / Moments` and the cluster accelerations, capacity per `PartJointSpec`, breaking via `Cut`; wiring `Cut` / `OnVesselSplit` /
`OnVesselMerge` into Part.decouple / Undock / Couple / joint breaks; autostrut rebuild on vessel change; Heaviest anchors"). **No golden or
capture covers joint loads or breaking** (PhysX's joint solve is not reproducible and the reduced model has no joint compliance to compare): the
gate is the KSP capacity numbers bit for bit against an independent reference built from the in-game part database, the load model against an
independent numpy reference, analytic break loads, the spike's own load / capacity numbers, scenarios through the game events with momentum
bookkeeping, and determinism. Every existing gate is unchanged (`harness/compare/tolerances.json`, `tests/tolerances_capture.json` untouched).

### What is in

| piece | files | KSP source |
|---|---|---|

Jolt's manifold reduction merges the manifolds of different sub-shapes of a body pair and reports only the first in OnContactAdded / Persisted, so the listener takes the touching sub-shapes from `OnContactValidate` (called per sub-shape hit before the merge; it accepts everything), and a pair served from Jolt's body-pair cache keeps its last set; mutex-guarded, sorted after the step (thread-count independent). `CompoundBodyDesc::useManifoldReduction` exposes Jolt's per-body switch (left on) |

### Exact / approximate / changed, per choice

| choice | class | notes |
|---|---|---|
| capacity per sub-joint (breakingForce / Torque, the PhysX limits with JointBreak*Factor and the rigid factors), stiffness, sub-joint count, node choice | exact | bit-identical to the independent reference from the in-game part database |
| the break rule: a ConfigurableJoint breaks when its own force or torque exceeds its limit; the whole PartJoint goes and the child decouples (OnJointBreak); IgnoreCollisionsFrames keeps the part, only the broken sub-joints go | exact rule | evaluated after the step from the step's loads (PhysX: inside its solve) |
| the load of a sub-joint | approximate | quasi-static, from the clusters' rigid-body motion over the step; elastic split with a uniform quasi-rigid linear stiffness and KSP's angular drives |
| tree solve on tree craft | exact statics | equal to the articulated impulses (S 0.53 %, M2 0.07 % max) |
| graph solve with struts / autostruts / several supports | approximate | elastic sharing; PhysX's own split is iteration-order dependent (R1) |
| ground supports | approximate | one support per touching part at its centre of mass (linear kLinear, rotational 1e8 kN m/rad), the cluster's residual carried elastically; Jolt's contact impulses are not read per part |
| Heaviest walk, its tie rules and per-part cache, Root / Grandparent anchors, the symmetry loop | exact rules | cache keyed by the physics step count (= Time.fixedTime); the NRE of a cache hit modelled as "no autostrut this cycle" |
| CycleAutoStrut timing (release at once, secure after the next step) | exact | welds for autostruts that cross clusters are made at securing |
| decouple / undock / couple / dock / part death / vessel modified -> rebind | exact conservation | every new cluster takes the momentum of its parts; batched per frame |
| the onPartJointBreak `breakForce` | approximate | Unity passes OnJointBreak a force; here the broken sub-joint's breakForce (positive, so OnPartJointBreak takes the same branch) |
| which parts are supports | exact for the proxy colliders | every sub-shape within 1 mm of static geometry (Jolt's per-hit validation); the contact solve itself is unchanged (manifold reduction on, WP-20b's numbers bit for bit) |

### Known deviations from joint-flex KSP (honest list)

- **No joint compliance**: KSP's PartJoints are rigid linear drives with angular springs; bending a tall stack under load moves load (the
  articulated M2 already carries 2,263 kN m of bending at the Mainsail at 1 g that the rigid model does not have), wobble and oscillation-driven
  failures exist. Here the loads are the quasi-static loads of the rigid motion: tall unstrutted stacks are STRONGER than in KSP under high
  static load (the spike's capacity bench: M2 first breaks at 29 g here, 10.8 g articulated; M2-AS 25.1 g here, 18.8 g articulated; the short
  S breaks at the same 33.7 g in all models). Risk R2 of PHYSICS-SPIKE.md, accepted with the reduced model.
- **Impacts** (landing, docking at speed, collisions): a contact resolved in one step is a one-step acceleration spike, so a hard contact reads
  as a large quasi-static load; PhysX spreads it through the joint springs over a few steps. The scenarios' 5 cm placement drop would break
  L2-AS's Mainsail joint at touchdown without the 60-tick grace the spike used (KSP: `ignoreCollisionsFrames = 60` after its exact landed
  placement, Vessel.cs:2543).
- **Load sharing between parallel paths** (struts, autostruts, docking loops, several supports) follows the elastic model, not PhysX's
  iteration order: the first joint to break can differ from KSP's on strutted craft (gate by scenario, PHYSICS-SPIKE.md R1).
- **Re-rooted / coupled joints**: Part.Couple and SetHierarchyRoot create the new attach joints with the target's / root's `attachMode`
  (Part.cs:3194, :3232); a rebound binding builds each joint with the part's own `attachMode`, so a joint that KSP made as STACK can be
  SRF_ATTACH here (or the reverse): its stiffness and num3 (capacity) differ until the vessel is reloaded (KSP rebuilds it with the own mode then).
- **Same-vessel docking joints** (`DockingEnvironment::createSameVesselJoint`) and robotic servos are no elements of the graph (WP-25 / WP-52).
- After a rebind the new bindings report loads from their first full step on; partial PartJoints (some sub-joints destroyed) exist only on the
  IgnoreCollisionsFrames path, as in KSP.

### Risks

- R1 (cost): the graph solve is the largest item of the structural layer (L2-AS 0.093 ms, XL2-AS 0.44 ms per tick in Release); a float or
  AVX2 block kernel, or solving only the joints near capacity, are the levers if it matters.
- R2 (impacts): see the deviations; a host that lands vessels must place them as KSP does (exact ground placement + ignoreCollisionsFrames).
- R3 (supports): the PhysProf crafts stand on ONE proxy box (the core Mainsail's); with the .mu colliders (R6) more parts will touch and the
  support split will matter more.
- R4: Windows vs Linux bit-identity is not measured (the tests compare inside one process).

## WP-19b: frames and the physics bubble (branch `wp19b`, from local `wp20b` 950c1d94)

State: done for the engine-agnostic part. Scope = the WP-20b "Deferred to WP-19b" list (frame-origin policy and the R1 frame-mixing risk, the
rotating / inertial switch of the bodies, Vessel.ChangeWorldVelocity incl. krakensbaneAcc, the Krakensbane host, FloatingOrigin consistent with
the reduced model, several vessels in one bubble, the bindings' lifecycle) and PHYSICS-SPIKE.md section 7 row WP-19b (`frame_switch`,
`two_vessels`). **No golden or capture covers rigid bodies in the flight scene** (PhysX is not reproducible): the gate is an independent Python
reference for every bit-exact piece (0 ULP), analytic scenarios against an independent two-body propagator (not kspcore's Orbit), and invariance
checks. Every existing gate is unchanged (`harness/compare/tolerances.json`, `tests/tolerances_capture.json` untouched). WP-20c's files (load
graph, Cut / Merge internals) are not touched.

### The frame policy (resolves WP-20b risk R1)

kspcore's world had the dominant body at the origin (Kerbin's reversed orbit driver, position 0), so a vessel in orbit had float fields 700 km
from the origin (6 cm ulp) and CalculatePhysicsStats' `CoM = CoMD; localCoM = vesselTransform.InverseTransformPoint(CoM)` either lost 1-6 cm
(`floatOrigin` 0) or mixed frames (`floatOrigin` near the vessel). Decided:

1. **One world frame** for every float and double world position, KSP's convention (`floatOrigin` stays 0): transforms, Vessel.CoM,
   rb.worldCenterOfMass, AddForceAtPosition's position, CelestialBody.position, Vessel.CoMD. Every ported statement runs unchanged.
2. **Its origin follows the active vessel** by FloatingOrigin's own decision (FloatingOrigin.cs:131-145: `continuous`, or the active vessel
   farther than `threshold` 500 m, while canEngageThisFrame) and setOffset's own shift (FloatingOrigin.cs:181-206: bodies, vessels'
   SetPosition, CoMD / CoM) applied to the **non-physics** state only (`PhysicsBubble::ShiftWorld`). Jolt bodies never move for it: they are tied
   to the world by one double, `FrameOriginWorld` (the world position of the physics origin), which the shift moves with everything else.
   Measured: localCoM 1.3 cm off with the vessel 720 km from the origin, 1e-7 m after the rebase; in orbit the rebase happens every ~12 ticks
   (50 in 12 s), the transform stays within 532 m of the origin, the trajectory equals a run without rebases to 1.2e-6 m.
3. **Krakensbane's frame drift** stays WP-20a's FrameOffset (no per-tick shift: KSP's per-tick branch FloatingOrigin.cs:146-150 is not a trigger).
   Dynamic bodies are at world = FrameOriginWorld + p + FrameOffset, **static geometry at FrameOriginWorld + s** (the body frame). The two agree
   only while FrameOffset is zero, so: static collisions are OFF while it is not (`PhysicsWorld::SetStaticCollisions`; KSP's SafeToEngage keeps
   every loaded vessel 150-200 m above the terrain while Krakensbane is engaged), and the drift is FOLDED into the dynamic bodies (one SetPosition
   per body) as soon as the frame velocity is zero again (Krakensbane.Zero, packed active vessel). Without the gate a body at rest 5 m above a
   static floor while the frame drifts 20 m was hit by the stale floor (20.5 m of disturbance); with it: 6e-7 m, then it lands on the real floor.
4. **The physics origin** is re-centred on the active vessel (every Jolt body moved once, O(bodies)) only past `physicsOriginRebaseDistance`
   1,000 km (PHYSICS-SPIKE.md R3, Jolt's float broad phase); trajectories equal to 1.4e-7 m with / without, static bodies' world positions exact.
5. Rotating <-> inertial and the SOI change do not move the physics origin: the world axes are KSP's (body-fixed in the rotating frame, inertial
   otherwise) and the dominant body stays still in the world (the reversed orbit-driver chain): only velocities change, as the C# changes them.

Static meshes (WP-12b terrain quads, WP-42 KSC) must be added at `PhysicsBubble::StaticPhysicsFromWorld(world)`; terrain colliders are valid in the
rotating frame of their body (in the inertial regime the body turns under them: rebuild them on onRotatingFrameTransition, WP-12b).

### Findings (KSP behaviour reproduced; a later implementer must keep or knowingly change them)

- **Two clocks.** UT advances by Planetarium.fixedDeltaTime = 0.02 (double, Planetarium.cs:82 / :205), physics by Time.fixedDeltaTime = 0.02f
  (TimeWarp.cs:423), and VesselPrecalculate's drift compensation moves a vessel by TimeWarp.fixedDeltaTime along its Kepler orbit per tick: a
  vessel in physics runs 4.47e-10 s per tick behind the UT-clocked rails position (1 um per tick at 2.2 km/s, 1.7 cm in 335 s). The gates use
  the physics clock; it cancels between vessels.
- **Frame changes take one tick to reach the bodies' frame.** OrbitPhysicsManager.FixedUpdate (seq 280) switches the frame after Planetarium /
  CelestialBody.CBUpdate (seq 6) computed this tick's frame; the step (seq 291) then runs the new velocities in the old axes. The rotating <->
  inertial switch therefore turns the trajectory by omega dt about the body's axis once (-/+ (omega x r) dt: 3-4 m at 100 km on Kerbin), the SOI
  change leaves the vessel - new body distance one tick of the body's motion behind (-V dt: 10.8 m for the Mun). Both reproduced and gated as such.
- setRotatingFrame moves every part by omega x r_root (vessel.transform.position) and leaves angular velocities alone; krakensbaneAcc changes by
  rFrmVel itself (not / dt) there, by velOffset / dt in ChangeWorldVelocity. krakensbaneAcc is never read in Assembly-CSharp (mods only).
- The first orbitDriftFramesToWait (5) ticks after an unpack run without drift compensation (1.2 mm per tick of Euler error in the rotating frame,
  7.5 mm total), then the vessel is held on its orbit.

### Risks

- R1: the `two_vessels` relative error (0.65 mm of the 1 mm bound) is dominated by the float rounding of the other vessel's physics-frame velocity
  (~10 m/s relative, KSP's Krakensbane rule re-centres on the active vessel only); another compiler / platform may land closer to the bound.
- R2: the gate on static collisions relies on KSP's SafeToEngage (150-200 m clearance); a host that engages the frame velocity near terrain (the
  kspcore `recentreSpeed` option does not change when it engages) would lose ground contact while engaged.
- R3: the world rebase uses the active vessel's float transform (as KSP): after a rebase the vessel sits within the float rounding of its old
  position (1-2 cm at 700 km) of the origin, not exactly at it.
- R4: frame changes and their one-tick displacement are KSP's (findings above); an engine that wants them exact must change the tick order, not
  the bubble.

## WP-29b: KSP wheel part modules (branch `wp29b`, from local `wp29a` `2d90e6fe`; merged)

State: ModuleWheelBase, the ModuleWheels submodules and the SuspensionLoadBalancer are ported 1:1 from the decompiled C# and gated bit-exactly (0 ULP, NaN == NaN, the sign of zero included) against an independent Python reference, on top of the WP-29a VPP wheel core. Source of truth: `Assembly-CSharp/ModuleWheelBase.cs`, `ModuleWheels/*.cs`, `SuspensionLoadBalancer.cs`, `WheelType.cs`; scope and the quirks list: `core/WHEEL-SPIKE.md` (section 1.5 Q3, Q4, Q8, Q12 and section 7, WP-29b). WP-29c (the native WheelCollider, the PhysX suspension law, welding wheels into the rigid cluster) is not part of this package.

### Ported (`include/ksp/wheels/wheel_modules.hpp`, `src/wheels/wheel_modules.cpp`, `wheel_base.cpp`, `wheel_submodules.cpp`; every function carries a `File.cs:line` cite, `tools/wp28/check_cites.py` and `tools/wp55/check_cites.py` exact mode: 155 cites, 0 mismatches)
- `ModuleWheelBase`: `OnAwake`, `OnStart` (transform lookups, ForceHeaviest auto-strut, the deferred set-up coroutine `WaitUntil(part.started && !part.packed)`, event subscriptions, substeps, LEG `minimumDownforce = 10` and the `ki = 1000` rule), `WheelSetup` (controller creation, collider radius `radius * rescaleFactor`, layer mask, damping, `maxRpm`, `WheelOrgPosR / RotR`, sub-system cascade, gee bias, `tireFriction.model = Lineal`), `ApplyGeeBias` / `UpdateFriction`, `FixedUpdate` (slip displacement, damage hand-over, `isGrounded`, landing detection -> `GroundContact` / `GroundContacts` / `SetLandedAt` / `checkLanded`, `maxRpm`, drift fix, the rigid-body "schloompa" freeze with its delayed unfreeze), `OnPutToGround`, pack / unpack, docking / undocking handlers, `SOIChange`, inventory / promote / demote hooks, the sub-system enable / disable cascade (`InopWheelCollider`, `CheckSuspensionToggle`), `EvtAutoFrictionToggle`, `ActAutoFrictionToggle`, `ActionUIUpdate`.
- `WheelSubsystem(s)` (multicast `OnModified`), `WheelUtil` (`SpeedToRpm`, `RpmToSpeed`, `RpmToDegsSec`), `ModuleWheelSubmodule` (base resolution through `baseModuleIndex` or the first `ModuleWheelBase`, registration, `OnWheelInit`).
- `ModuleWheelMotor` (torque curve evaluated at `|angularVelocity * cfg radius|`, **torque rounded to 0.01 at set-up and every tick**, traction control, `driveLimiter`, `GetMotorOrientationSign`, `CheckMotorState` with the electric-charge draw through `resHandler.UpdateModuleResourceInputs`, adjusters), `ModuleWheelMotorSteering`, `ModuleWheelSteering` (coordinate frame, Ackermann turn centre, steering / max-angle curves, `SteeringRadius` part value), `ModuleWheelBrakes` (status light, adjusters), `ModuleWheelLock`, `ModuleWheelSuspension` (auto spring / damper, `BoostCurve`, auto boost, high-gee override, oscillation damper, `ResetSuspensionCollider`), `ModuleWheelDamage` (stress and impact model, repair, `Random`, IConstruction), `ModuleWheelDeployment` (the KerbalFSM Deployed / Retracting / Retracted / Deploying / Inoperable over the Unity `Animation`, `TsubSys` sub-system switch, `FindTransformAnimationTime`, toggle events and actions), `ModuleWheelBogey` (the managed math up to `bogeyRot`).
