### Gate (`tests/test_wheel_modules.cpp` + `tests/test_wheel_modules_derived.cpp`, 10 cases / 9,832 assertions; ctest `wheels.modules` runs the 10 `WP-29b*` cases; also part of `unit` and of the random-order runs)
- Reference: `tools/wp29b/wheel_reference.py` -> `tests/data/wp29b_reference.json` (11 MB, deterministic seeds; regenerate with `python -I tools/wp29b/wheel_reference.py > tests/data/wp29b_reference.json`).
- How circularity was avoided: the Python was written first, from the C# text only, with its own object model (plain Python objects, a generator-based coroutine scheduler, its own KerbalFSM, `Animation` and `FloatCurve` models, numpy float32 helpers), before any C++ of this package existed; the C++ was then written from the C# again, never from the Python. The inputs (control state, WheelState values, transforms, collider kinds, electric charge, events, bodies, warp rates, long ticks so the 30-90 s repair immunity runs out) are generated by the Python and only replayed by the C++; the stock wheel parameters are parsed by the Python from the part .cfg files of `core/testdata/GameData-mirror` and the C++ reads them through its own module host (`PartLoader` + `PartModule.Load`), so a parsing or default error shows as a mismatch. The gate found reference bugs (an input that skipped its float store, a doubled float store in `h = length * (1 / tan)`, `f`-suffixed literals used as doubles (0.2f, 0.85f, 0.8f ...), a trace that was not cleared, the 2-value `AddKey` smoothing missing from the curve model) and port bugs (an enum field read as `int`, `0.01f` / `0.2f` / `0.4f` / `0.025f` / `57.29578f` / `0.02f` written as doubles, engine-call traces at the wrong places), all fixed on the side that deviated from the C#. Mutation checks (radius quirk, torque rounding at set-up and per tick, the damper constant, stress timing, the gee formula, the steering last-input, the sign of `wDot`) are all caught.
- Sweeps: (1) `WheelUtil`: 300 rows x 3 functions. (2) `ApplyGeeBias`: 13 stock wheel parts x 5 gee x autoFriction x model {cfg, new, old} x geeBias {cfg, 1.6, 2.0} x with / without controller = 2,340 rows. (3) `OnPutToGround`: 78 rows (retracted gear, ground-height offset). (4) `SuspensionLoadBalancer.FixedUpdate`: 400 random vessels (1-9 wheels, landed or not, gravity multiplier, min mass). (5) 39 runs (every stock wheel part x gee 1.0 / 0.166 / 1.67 x physics-warp rate 1 / 2 / 4), 200 ticks each, in the order events -> coroutine pass + `Deployment.Update` -> `FixedUpdate` of every module in cfg order -> `Animation` tick -> `LateUpdate` -> `PartValues.Update`: 16 numeric sections per tick (controller inputs, collider spring / damper / geometry, base, motor, steering, brakes, suspension, damage, deployment, lock, bogey) and the ordered trace of the engine calls, also right after set-up; 11 MB of expected values, d.total > 500,000 compared values. Events scripted per run: brake, motor toggles / traction control, gear action / event (retract and deploy cycles), auto-friction event / action, steering toggle, spring-damper toggle, suspension enable / disable, damage and repair, pack / unpack, SOI change, docking / undocking, startup-time reset.
- Derived cases (from the C# control flow, labelled in `test_wheel_modules_derived.cpp`): `SOIChange` never applies, `ActAutoFrictionToggle`'s inverted test, the `LandedDetectionNeedsUpdate` truth table, `baseModuleIndex` resolution and its error log, Save / Load round trip of every persistent field of every wheel module of the 13 stock parts, `Deployment.OnLoad / CopySerializedFrom / OnSave`, adjusters chain order, the impact-damage enable table, IConstruction.

### Findings kept from the C#
- `ModuleWheelBase.SOIChange` compares `FromTo.from` (a CelestialBody) with `base.vessel` (a Vessel) through `UnityEngine.Object.operator ==`: always false, so the gee bias is never re-applied on an SOI change (the friction multiplier keeps the value of the body the wheel was set up on). Kept.
- `ActAutoFrictionToggle` / `ActAutoTorqueToggle`: `x = act.type != Activate || (act.type == Toggle && !x)`: an Activate action turns the feature OFF and Deactivate / Toggle turn it ON. Kept.
- The M1 radius quirk (Q3): the collider radius is `radius * rescaleFactor` (1.25 default) while the slip displacement, the motor torque curve and `maxRpm` use the cfg `radius`. Kept and gated (a mutation of `slipDisplacement.y` to the collider radius fails on the first run). `ModuleWheelBase.FixedUpdate` writes `wheel.maxRpm = SpeedToRpm(wheelMaxSpeed, radius)` every tick, so the `wheelSpeedMax`-based value the motor sets once at set-up lasts one tick (the order of the two writes depends on the Unity script order, assumed).
- Torque rounding (Q4): `Math.Round(torque * 100) / 100` at set-up and every tick; `ModuleWheelMotorSteering.GetMotorEnabled` never assigns `state` (stale `Disabled` / `Idle`); `GetMotorOrientationSign` always takes its second candidate (the first, `up . up`, can never win against `float.MinValue`).
- `ModuleWheelSteering.updateSteering`: `acos` of a non-negative `max(dot(right, s), dot(left, s))` is at most 90 degrees, so the `> 90` / `< -90` folds are unreachable (not exercised; ported as written). `OnLoad` / `OnSave` are empty overrides.
- `ModuleWheelDamage`: the stress model is silent for `startupTime` (8 s, reset on every landing and vessel change) and, after a repair, for `repairImmunityTimeTotal` (30-90 s, `Random.Range`); `OnStart` and the one-frame delayed callback of `OnWheelSetup` each consume two `Random` draws; `Time.deltaTime` (not the fixed step) counts `startupTime` down.
- `ModuleWheelBase.OnStart` starts the set-up coroutine, which waits for `part.started && !part.packed` (Part.Start has finished) and runs in the next frame's coroutine pass: the set-up of a wheel happens after every module's `OnStart`.
- `Part.explode()`, ScreenMessages, `FlightLogger`, `InputLockManager` locks (taken through the real `InputLockManager`), collision-ignore, FX and drag-cube weights are recorded through `WheelModuleEnvironment::trace`; the drag-cube weights are applied to the part's real `DragCubeList`.

### Natives and seams (UNVERIFIED, no C# source exists)
- `AnimationCurve`: `AddKey(time, value)` re-derives the tangents of the new key and of both neighbours (`AddKeySmoothTangents`) and `Evaluate` uses the cached cubic in polynomial form. The Python transcribes both from the capture-verified WP-01 port (`src/unity/animation_curve.cpp`), so this is the one place where the reference is not independent; it matters because 2-value `key =` lines in the stock `steeringCurve` (all stock steering wheels) go through it.
- `PartTransform` / `Vessel.ReferenceTransform` maths (`rotation * Scale(1, p) + position`, `up`, `forward`: managed Mono-rule operators as in WP-13; the native matrix rounding order is not captured) and the WP-29a `NativeTransform` (`right` for `wLeft0`, `forward` / `right` for the drift fix): both implementations follow the same documented formulation.
- `Animation` clock (`time += speed * dt`, `ClampForever`; WP-27) and the coroutine scheduler semantics (a `yield null` resumes in a later frame's pass, `WaitForSeconds` on the scheduler clock; WP-00): documented Unity behaviour, not observed.
- `Quaternion.AngleAxis`: the test rebinds `NativeOps::AngleAxis` to the reference's formulation (as WP-29a); the production binding is the capture-verified UCRT one.
- Module order: FixedUpdate / Update / LateUpdate run in cfg order and the animation ticks after FixedUpdate: the Unity script order of the part modules, the runtime-added `KSPWheelController` and the load balancer is unknown (WHEEL-SPIKE R5, capture C11c).
- `Bogey`: `Quaternion.RotateTowards` / `Lerp` onto `bogey.localRotation` (native) and the wheel-spin copy to `wheelTrfs` are not ported: the host writes `bogeyLocalRotation` from `bogeyRot`; `bogeyAngle`, `bogeyUp` and `bogeyRot` are gated.

### Not ported
`GetInfo` / `OnGatherInfo` / `GetModuleDisplayName` text and the PAW UI (slider limits, `UIPartActionController` checks), `CacheLocalStrings`, `Debug.DrawRay` gizmos, `VPWheelCollider.AdjustToWheelMesh` (no stock part sets `FitWheelColliderToMesh`), `GetDragCubeNames` / `AssumeDragCubePosition`, the EVA repair kit inventory and skill checks of `EventRepairExternal` (the repair itself is `SetDamaged(false)`), `ModuleStatusLight` and `ModuleLight` as classes (the wheel modules use the `IWheelStatusLight` seam; the stock gear's `slaveModules = 8` therefore resolves to no `IScalarModule` yet, so `SetScalar(0)` / `SetUIWrite` on the light are not exercised), `part.UpdateAutoStrut`, `Vessel.cs:2600-2640` (the ground-height collider search of vessel placement: needs the colliders of WP-29c; the anchor exceptions at `:1565` already exist from WP-14).

### Residual risks
- The AnimationCurve transcription above; every stock `steeringCurve` has 2-value keys.
- Module and coroutine order (R5) and the frame model of the replay are assumptions; real captures (C11) may show a different order of `wheel.maxRpm` / `wheel.gravity` writes between the modules.
- The resource draw is the real WP-15 flow over one tank (the Python models a single store: `got = min(request, amount)`); a vessel with several tanks, priorities or crossfeed is not part of the gate.
- A 1 ULP double difference of `Math.Tan` / `Math.Acos` / `Math.Pow` between the lifted VS2013 CRT (C++) and the host libm (Python) landing on a float rounding boundary would show as a 1 ULP mismatch; none occurs in the gate.
- Not pushed; the unit suite was not run on the clang toolchain.

### Runs

### Findings (a later implementer must know)

- **KSP's orbit-drift compensation stays engaged while an engine burns in vacuum**: the orbit is refitted to the rigid body every frame, so the
  drift check passes; gravity is the exact Kepler step of the tick, the thrust is integrated on top (burn test: 500 / 500 ticks).
- **The centre of mass moves inside a vessel as its tanks drain** (VesselPhysics keeps the parts' motion): -0.167 m along the axis in 10 s for the
  Mainsail stack. A point-mass reference must follow a rigid point (the root part), not CoMD.
- **The WP-20b `World` fixture never runs PhysicsGlobals.Start**, so `bodyLiftCurve` is the empty default and every DragCubeList made afterwards has
  no body lift: the WP-20b / WP-19b scenarios ran without body lift. WP-20d's fixtures set it (`StartPhysicsGlobals`) before making crafts.
- kspcore has **no flight-scene resource-flow host**: ResourceFlowEnvironment::vesselHost and Vessel::env.updateResourceSets are seams (the tests
  wire VesselResourceSets as test_staging.cpp does); without them the engines throw at UpdatePropellantStatus.
- Module FixedUpdates check `loadedScene == FLIGHT` (SaveEnvironment); the WP-19b `BubbleScene` leaves MAINMENU. WP-20d's scenes set FLIGHT.
- Part.Start's 288 K block never fires for a part whose temperature is -1: the external-temperature assignment just above it replaces it first
  (Part.cs:1825-1849); kept.
- CalculateConstantsAtmosphere multiplies `solarFlux` by the atmospheric multiplier every FixedUpdate and only FlightIntegrator.Update resets it
  (two ticks in one frame compound it); kept.
- PhysProf-S and -M2 are aerodynamically unstable past Mach ~0.9 without SAS (AoA 0.6 deg at 2.5 km, 2.6 deg at Mach 1, tumbling after; S tumbles
  at 9 s, as it did in KSP's own capture with SAS on).
- C10's frame 0 is not our ignition tick: our states come 26-30 frames later at the same altitudes with the same speeds (the KSC launch pad
  surface is ~7.6 m above the PQS terrain the craft stands on here: PhysProf-S's root is at 79.29 m in C6, 71.65 m here; there are no KSC
  colliders yet: WP-42 / WP-12b). Only offset-free quantities are gated.
- With the real FlightIntegrator the WP-19b scenarios move slightly (rb.angularDrag 0 in vacuum, set by UpdateAerodynamics): two_vessels 0.49 mm
  (was 0.65), frame_switch residual 0.27 mm (was 0.3).

### Merge with main (WP-20c, WP-19b, WP-12b, WP-29b, WP-32): WP-20c's loads in the tick, the L2-AS pad failures

With `origin/main` merged, WP-20c's load solve and PhysX break rule run in every `VesselPhysics::AfterStep` of the bubble, under the
FlightIntegrator's forces. `unit.shard.2` and `unit.random_order.27` then failed on the two L2-AS launches from the pad: SoA == exact
`partTicks 657,511 != 730,743` (= 7 ticks x 457 parts + 1,592 x 411), 1,089 m after 30 s (pad + 1,000 m required), the C10 ascent -24.5 % speed at
1 km with 10.5 deg AoA and no 2.5 km state.

- **Not the flight loads.** The engines' thrust reaches the load solve as KSP's PartJoints carry it (ModuleEngines -> Part.AddForceAtPosition at the
  thrust transforms on the engine part -> Integrate's buffers -> that part's node, carried by its attach joint), the aero forces likewise on every
  part. Over the 30 s powered flights the largest sub-joint load is 0.148 of capacity (S, its radial decoupler, tumbling) and 0.044 (M2-AS and
  L2-AS, the radial decouplers at the end of the burn): WP-20c's own ascents gave 0.046 for L2-AS.
- **The pad touchdown.** L2-AS broke at tick 7 of the 100-tick settle, 93 ticks before ignition: the core Mainsail's attach sub-joint at 28,861 kN
  (breakForce 20,000) and five radial decouplers at 1,912-2,502 kN (1,760); 46 of 457 parts (the core Mainsail, five boosters) left as debris and
  the rest flew without its core engine. The WP-20d `PadScene` dropped the craft 5 cm onto the pad at full gravity (about 1 m/s at contact); the
  contact stops the 680 t vessel in one 20 ms step and WP-20c's quasi-static loads, which have no joint compliance (WP-20c's "Impacts" deviation),
  put that impulse through the one supporting proxy box (0.82 of capacity the tick before the break; M2 / M2-AS took 0.47 / 0.35 at their
  touchdown). KSP's launch has no such impact; the fixture differed from it twice:
  1. its OrbitDriver was never started. Unity runs OrbitDriver.Start (OrbitDriver.cs:98) before the vessel's first FixedUpdate (the WP-19b
     PlaceOnOrbit does it, PadScene::Place did not); without `ready` UpdateOrbit returns at once (:152), lastMode never records IDLE (:156, the
     packed frame's call VesselPrecalculate.cs:186), so CalculateGravity's physics easing (VesselPrecalculate.cs:290-302, PHYSICS_EASE on: gravity
     0 -> 1 in steps of 1 / 16 after IDLE -> TRACK_Phys) never started, and in flight the orbit was not tracked from the bodies;
  2. it put the lowest proxy corner 5 cm above the pad point, where Vessel.GoOffRails of a spawning landed vessel runs CheckGroundCollision
     (Vessel.cs:2418, :2493-2576) and puts the lowest collider point on the ground below.
  Easing alone still broke the Mainsail joint (27,842 kN at tick 12: the same drop under the ramp); the exact placement alone left 0.66 of
  capacity; both: 0.37, which is L2-AS's static 1 g load on its single support (WP-20c's pad ramp breaks that joint at 2.98 g).
- **Fix (tests only, `tests/flight_integrator_fixture.hpp`)**: Place sets the lowest proxy point on the pad and starts the OrbitDriver (CoMD set
  first to CalculatePhysicsStats' packed landed value, VesselPrecalculate.cs:469-480). No grace period, no tolerance or gate changed. New checks:
  no joint break and every part kept on the pad and in the nine 30 s flights and up to the last C10 state compared; flight max load / capacity < 1
  (reported); lastMode IDLE after the packed tick and gravityMultiplier 1 / 16 in the first unpacked one. `~PadScene` clears
  `Vessel::SpawnedVessels` (a break's debris would otherwise outlive the World whose part database its parts use).
- Effect: the settled crafts sit 1.9 cm lower (Jolt's 2 cm penetration slop without an impact: S root 71.649 m, was 71.668); the C10 numbers moved
  by at most 0.3 percentage points (Gate table); after 30 s S 3,837 m (tumbling; was 3,907), M2-AS 4,782 m, L2-AS 2,468 m.
- Not modelled: CheckGroundCollision also sets ignoreCollisionsFrames = 60 on some branches (Vessel.cs:2543 / :2551 / :2557), during which the host
  keeps a broken part in its vessel (PartJoint.cs:399); nothing comes near capacity on the pad now, so the fixture does not set it.
- **`test_flight3.cpp:382` in the `-rs=27` failure list** (WP-19a VesselSwitching.Update returned nothing in 5 scenes): an order dependence, not this
  package's. Bisected to `WP-32 parachute states` (tests/test_eva_behaviour2.cpp:254): its walk over the KerbalEVA states sets
  `ControlPanelLock_<id>` (every control but UI / camera, KerbalEVA.cs:2419) without the state's OnLeave, and VesselSwitching.Update returns at the
  VESSEL_SWITCHING lock (VesselSwitching.cs:37) in every later case; the two cases alone reproduce it. The hygiene listener now resets
  InputLockManager's lock stack between cases (`KSP_HYGIENE_TRACE=1` names the case that left a lock).

### Risks

- R1: the ascent gate is KSP's own flight but only up to Mach 1 / 5 km (no SAS in this tick); beyond that our crafts turn away. Wiring
  FeedInputFeed (WP-24 / WP-50) would extend it to C10's 20 km / 36.7 km states.
- R2: `StartPartsInFlight` is the subset of Part.Start the tick reads; module OnStart (ModulesOnStart) is the host's module lifecycle (the module-slot
  test starts its surfaces itself).
- R3: the default sun input of the thermal half is analytic (no scaled-space colliders): direct-sunlight decisions near a limb may differ by the
  collider shapes.

How the proxies map: BoxCollider -> Box (|size x lossyScale| / 2, the node's rotation), SphereCollider -> Sphere (radius x largest |scale|), CapsuleCollider -> Capsule (radius x larger non-axis |scale|, height x axis |scale|, an X / Z capsule rotated into Jolt's Y by -90 / +90 degrees), MeshCollider -> Jolt `ConvexHullShape` of the part-space vertices (KSP forces every mesh collider convex), triggers and wheel markers dropped (a trigger has no contact response and PhysX leaves it out of the mass properties). Mass properties for the per-part inertia tensor (`Part.cs:1890` stand-in) are the analytic capsule integrals and Jolt's hull integrals (volume, centroid, full tensor); a set of boxes keeps the previous code path bit for bit. `MuPartColliders::Hook()` plugs into `VesselPhysicsOptions::colliders`: parts with readable model data get their real colliders, every other part keeps the labelled FIXTURE (`DragCubeColliderProxy`); `stats()` counts both paths. Models are read from `Part::models[i].file->fullPath()` (the files PartLoader resolved); the test GameData mirror holds 0-byte `.mu` placeholders, so on the mirror every part takes the fixture path.

Linux (clang / gcc, sanitizers) not run locally: CI.

### Findings

- **Meshes are not all convex solids.** Qhull's hull of the collider vertices differs from the volume of the mesh triangles by 1.7 to 12 % for four colliders (Poodle `Col1` / `Col2`, turboFanEngine `TRJCOL1` / `TRJCOL2`; one hull is 4 % smaller than the mesh solid: the mesh is open or inverted in places), so the triangle solid is the wrong mass model; PhysX / Unity use the hull, and so does this port (Jolt hull integrals).
- Tags: `NoAttach` (SRB5 / SRB10 `COL2`, turboFanEngine `TRJCOL2`) only matters to the editor's attach raycasts; the colliders still collide. Layer is 0 on every stock engine collider. Triggers: none among the 19 engines.
- Native quaternion product: `UnityNative::Multiply` associates `w` as `(lw*rw - lx*rx) - (ly*ry + lz*rz)` (the WP-17b empirical fit, UNVERIFIED); the WP-17b python `qmul` associates it `lw*rw - ((lx*rx + ly*ry) + lz*rz)`. They differ only in rounding (a 7e-14 noise `w` of the omsEngine collider moved by 58,000 float ULP of that tiny number). The mucollider reference carries its own `qmul` with the C++ association; WP-17's python is untouched.
- Gimbal colliders: `liquidEngine*` colliders sit under gimbal transforms; the cluster compound holds them at the rest pose (no animation in the rigid-body model).

### Blocker (precise)

The permission layer denied every read of `decompiled/KSP-dev/**` in this session (Read, Glob and Bash all refused). Only the 19 engine models staged earlier into `core/data/mu_staging` (WP-17b, sha256 manifest) could be used. Consequences:

1. **Stock-part collider counts for all 362 parts were NOT checked.** The 19 engines are checked (31 colliders, 1 to 3 per part, no part without a body collider, no trigger). Next step: `python -I core/tools/mucollider/sweep_stock_parts.py --game decompiled/KSP-dev --out core/data/mucollider_stock_counts.json` (resolves MODEL nodes or the directory's first `.mu`, parses with the python reference, fails on parts without a non-trigger collider or with a mesh collider Qhull cannot hull; directories with several `.mu` and no MODEL node are listed as AMBIGUOUS because the file order is `UrlDir`'s; MODEL `rotation` is noted, not applied). The sweep logic was exercised on the 19 staged parts in a fake tree (9 resolvable parts passed; the others need the real directory layout).
2. **KSC / city scenery colliders were NOT extracted.** `tools/mucollider/extract_scenery_colliders.py` is written and unrun (and `harness/lib`, `harness/tools-cache` are not on this machine). Colliders are native Unity classes, so UnityPy reads them without type trees; the city objects are not in `sharedassets9.assets` alone (the PQSCity prefab's `renderers` / `objects` resolve to null with only that file loaded), so the script loads the whole `KSP_x64_Data`. Next step: run it with the harness venv (`<harness>/tools-cache/venv/Scripts/python.exe -I tools/mucollider/extract_scenery_colliders.py <KSP_x64_Data> <harness lib> core/data/scenery/scenery_colliders.json`), fix what the first run reports (UnityPy mesh accessors differ by version), add the `lod` table from the PQSCity / PQSCity2 MonoBehaviours (extract_terrain.py's type-tree method; the script writes `lod: []` and says so), then the existing test picks the file up (`data/scenery/scenery_colliders.json`: loads, builds, non-empty) and hosts call `ApplySceneryLod(PQSCityColliders&, city)` / `ApplySceneryLod(PQSCity2Colliders&, city)`.

with 4 substeps at 4x 0.41 / 0.51 ms per 0.08 s tick (the spike: 6-13 us per rover tick for the wheel part alone).

### Findings (a later implementer must know)

- **kspcore leaves Part.packed alone in GoOnRails / GoOffRails** (the `packPart` / `unpackPart` seams only build / drop bodies); ModuleWheelBase's
  set-up waits for `!part.packed` and never ran. The host mirrors the flag for wheel parts (with OnPartPack / OnPartUnpack); a general Part.Pack /
  Unpack (onPartPack / onPartUnpack events for every part) belongs to the vessel tick (WP-20e or later).
- **GameSettings' wheel block is zero until GameSettings.SetDefaultValues runs** (WHEEL_SUBSTEPS_ACTIVE 0: VPP integrates with 0 substeps, no tyre
  force at all). A host must run SetDefaultValues (or load settings.cfg); the test fixture sets KSP's defaults (GameSettings.cs:1059-1067).
- **ModuleWheelSteering needs Part.Update's PartValues refresh** (Part.Start sets overrideSkillUpdate for a part with ModuleWheelSteering or ModuleSAS,
  Part.cs:1915-1923; Part.Update then runs partValues.Update(), Part.cs:4328, which calls GetCoMFwdLength): without it CoMfwdLength stays 0 and a
  front wheel steers the wrong way. The host runs it for wheel parts; ModuleSAS parts need the same from their owner.
- PhysX applies the vehicle forces as a velocity change before its solver (updateNoDrive's integrateBody), with Unity's one substep the same as a
  force over the step; the managed WheelHit is the one of the previous step (as in Unity: VPP adds rb.velocity dt to its point).
- PhysX's **sticky-tyre constraints** (PxVehicleSuspLimitConstraintShader.h:145-190: below 0.2 m/s for 1 s the wheel is held by velocity rows) are
  not modelled: whether Unity's WheelCollider activates them is unknown. They would stop the slow creep of an unbraked rover (centrifugal, 8.6e-5 m/s^2
  at KSC); capture C11a (an unbraked rover at rest) settles it.
- The Prospector understeers at speed (10 m/s, 5 deg: yaw rate 64 % of kinematic): VPP's tyre saturates; at 2.5 m/s it is kinematic within 0.4 %.

Findings from the data (cfg and models, all 13 parts):
- Only the wheel collider NODE's transform matters to physics: `ModuleWheelBase.wheelSetup` overwrites radius, centre, suspension, spring, damper, mass and the friction curves of the chunk's component (`VPWheelCollider.SetupWheelCollider` zeroes both curves). The chunk's values are read where the component exists before the set-up: `Vessel.getLowestPoint`. The LT-1 / LT-2 legs carry NO WheelCollider chunk (`KSPWheelController.Create` adds the component); 11 of 13 parts carry one.
- Part colliders are on layer 26 "WheelCollidersIgnore" (the wheel ray ignores them, they collide), the wheel collider nodes on layer 27 "WheelColliders". Chain scale of every wheel collider node is 1.
- Landing gear and legs: `deployTgt` (an animated transform) is where `ModuleWheelDeployment` puts the wheel collider (`SetWheelTransform` at set-up and in every state callback); the LT-2's collider axis is 35 degrees off the vertical (the splayed leg), the gear bays' hang below the bay.
- `VPWheelCollider.UpdateVisualWheel` moves the suspension, caliper and wheel transforms to the current suspension position every frame; colliders below them (the tyre meshes `collider` / `collisionEnhancer`, the foot pistons) move with it in KSP. The cluster compound is static, so those subtrees and the collider `ModuleWheelSuspension` disables (`suspensionColliderName`) are left out of the cluster (the rover rests on its suspension, not on a frozen tyre mesh); the static hull remains. Left out: colliders that follow the suspension (tyre contacts with obstacles, a foot piston grazing rock).

### The wheel host on the models (`WheelPhysicsOptions::models`)

`FindModelTransform` answers from the rig (the collider host, the deploy target, suspension, steering pivots ...; refreshed from the part pose every sync); the collider host is a node of the model until `wheelSetup`, then rides on the part (Transform.SetParent keeps the world pose); a `SetWheelTransform` of `ModuleWheelDeployment` is written back as the new part-space pose. `findModelAnimator` / `sampleAnimation` give the module a `ksp::Animation` per clip holder; the clips advance in the physics step (`animatePhysics`, `TickAnimations`) and are sampled onto the rig. The hub colliders weld into the cluster at the part's animation state (stateString / position); the retracted gear's stand-in (`ModuleWheelDeployment.standInCollider`: a sphere of the wheel collider radius at `deployTgt`) is a sphere in the compound, followed in 5 cm steps by `VesselPhysics::Rebuild` (momentum-conserving). With no model library the WP-29c proxy path runs unchanged.

### Landed placement (`Vessel.cs:2578-2640` getLowestPoint's wheel branch)

`VesselEnvironment::colliderClosestPoints` (new): the collider scan with roles; `Vessel::getLowestPoint` now subtracts a WheelCollider's radius and 0.15, and 0.15 for a `collisionEnhancer`. The host answers for wheel parts from the rig: every non-trigger collider not on layers 21 / 16 / 20, the layer 26 / 27 / 30 ones temporarily enabled (so the colliders ModuleWheelSuspension disabled count), the WheelCollider chunk's centre and radius. The Two-Stage Lander placed landed now rests with its tyre bottoms 5.8 cm from the ground (the foot colliders touch it); the first port placed it 0.53 m inside it. UNVERIFIED: that `WheelCollider.bounds.min.z` is the collider's centre (the C# subtracts the radius afterwards, which is only right for a point).

## WP-52: Breaking Ground robotics (branch `wp52`, from main `cd5e4df4`)

State: done for the engine-agnostic part; the joint drive is a documented seam (decision below; WP-52b built its Jolt backend, see "WP-52b"). Scope = `Assembly-CSharp/Expansions/Serenity/` BaseServo.cs,
ModuleRoboticServoHinge.cs, ModuleRoboticServoPiston.cs, ModuleRoboticServoRotor.cs, ModuleRoboticRotationServo.cs, ModuleRoboticController.cs,
ControlledAxis.cs, ControlledAction.cs, RoboticControllerManager.cs (7,390 C# lines with ControlledBase / RoboticCollisions / IRoboticServo, which WP-53 had
ported), plus `ConfigurableJointExtensions.cs`. **No golden or capture covers a servo** (the SquadExpansion servo parts are not installed in the GameData
mirror or the dev copy: no `ModuleRoboticServo*` cfg exists, no in-game log of a servo): the gate is an independent Python reference at 0 ULP for every
piece of managed float maths, a double-precision algebra for the one joint formula, and labelled derived cases. Every existing gate is unchanged
(`harness/compare/tolerances.json`, `tests/tolerances_capture.json` untouched).

### Decision: the joint drive (WP-20b has no articulated bodies)

KSP drives a servo with a PhysX `ConfigurableJoint` that `BaseServo.OnJointInit` adds to the moving transform's GameObject (a D6 joint between the servo
`Rigidbody` and the part's): the module writes motions, limits, limit springs, drives (`positionSpring`, `positionDamper`, `maximumForce`),
`targetRotation` / `targetPosition` / `targetAngularVelocity` and PhysX integrates it. The reduced rigid-body model (WP-20b / c) has one Jolt body per
rigid cluster and **fixed** constraints between clusters only. Decided (2026-10-13):

1. The module logic is ported 1:1 and writes the joint's properties into **`ConfigurableJointData`** (`servo_joint.hpp`: the properties the five classes
   use, with the Unity defaults), the contract of the seam: an engine backend (a Jolt hinge / slider / motor constraint, the UE5 shell) reads it every
   physics step and drives the moving body. `SetTargetRotationLocal` (ConfigurableJointExtensions.cs, the only managed joint maths) is ported.
2. `HeadlessServoPlant` (`servo_modules.hpp`, `servo_plant.cpp`) is a **reference plant**, not PhysX: a 1-DOF model of the D6 drive (implicit spring /
   damper, force clamp `maximumForce`, hard limits, a vanishing limit spring means no limit, the shortest arc for unlimited joints; velocity drive for the
   rotor; linear drive for the piston) that moves the moving transform. SYNTHETIC inertia. It exists so the servo logic can be run closed loop in tests and
   headless, and it documents the drive law a backend must reproduce.
3. `ServoArticulation(PartJointSpec)` is the `VesselPhysicsOptions::isArticulation` hook: the joint a servo's moving side uses (`AttachServoRigidBody` /
   `NodeRigidBody` answer "servo body", PartJoint.SetupJoint cs:213-258) becomes an articulation point of the reduced model (tested on PhysProf-S: 2
   clusters and 1 constraint instead of 1 and 0). Until a backend gives that constraint a real hinge, the two bodies stay welded.
4. `BaseServo` is an `IJointLockState` and `Part.HasFreePivot` (`vessel_physics_joints.cpp`) asks it (IsJointUnlocked = !servoIsLocked, cs:1790).
5. The Unity side the modules touch is plain data supplied by the host: `ServoNode` (a Transform: local position / rotation, parent, world pose),
   `ServoBody` (the servo Rigidbody), `ServoRig` (the named model transforms `GameObject.GetChild(name)` finds). `BaseServo::angleSource` /
   `positionSource` let an engine that tracks the joint coordinate directly replace `currentTransformAngle()` (the native `localEulerAngles`); the gate
   uses them to feed scripted coordinates.

### Ported (`include/ksp/serenity/`, `src/serenity/`; every function carries a `File.cs:line` cite, `check_cites.py` exact: 289 cites, 0 mismatches)

- `BaseServo`: the whole class but the UI (below): OnAwake / OnLoad / OnSave / OnStart (transform lookups, `servoParentTransform` and its inverse,
  motorOutput, attach node transforms, the editor part sets, InitJoint), OnStartBeforePartAttachJoint (PostStartInitJoint), Promote / Demote, the
  FixedUpdate chain (rate-of-motion average over 20 readings, power draw `baseResourceConsumptionRate * motorOutput * rate / referenceConsumptionVelocity`
  or the velocity limit, `CalculateResourceDrain` with the power-loss disengage, the auto-restart on `HasEnoughResourcesToAutoStart`), Update (stopped-moving
  timer, `ApplyCoordsUpdate`), engage / disengage lock and motor, `ModifyServo` / `ModifyLocked` / `ManuallyModifyEngaged` (the events fire twice through
  the field event and the explicit call, as in C#), the axis field limits (`IAxisFieldLimits`), `GetModuleMass` / `GetModuleCost`, `AttachServoRigidBody`,
  `NodeRigidBody`, `ServoTransformCollider`, `VisualizeServo`, the editor part sets and spanning compound parts.
- `ModuleRoboticServoHinge` and `ModuleRoboticRotationServo`: target angle with soft / hard limits, `JointTargetAngle` (mirror, model offset, inverted), the
  per-tick `MoveTowards` (`MoveTowardsAngle` for full rotation) of the drive target at `traverseVelocity * fixedDeltaTime`, the joint drive and limit
  configuration (`driveSpringMutliplier` / `driveDampingMutliplier` from the motor output), the lock angle bookkeeping, power-loss lock, warp branches, mirror /
  symmetric handling (`CheckSymmetry`, `mirrorRotation`, `OnEditorPartEvent` + `OnVisualizeServo`), drag-cube weights (hinge), `ModifyLimitsMode`.
- `ModuleRoboticServoPiston`: extension / slave transforms / drag cubes / `UpdateCurrentExtension` through `servoParentTransformInverse` / `connectedAnchor`.
- `ModuleRoboticServoRotor`: RPM spool-up (`rotorSpoolTime`), brake mode, `SetJointDrive` in XYAndZ and slerp modes, direction / inversion, `RatchetLock`, load mass,
  the readout refresh.
- `ModuleRoboticController` (the sequencer): sequence position / length / play speed, direction, loop modes Once / Repeat / PingPong / OnceRestart with the
  action firing windows, the controlled axes and actions (add / remove / transfer to a symmetry partner / other-vessel cleanup / persistent id changes),
  the priority, persistence, play / stop / direction / loop events. `ControlledAxis` (time -> value `FloatCurve`, reverse / invert / rescale / align / clamp,
  the five stock presets Sine / Square / Triangle / Saw / RevSaw through `GenerateCurveFromReference`, `UpdateFieldValue`, symmetry fields),
  `ControlledAction` (times), `RoboticControllerManager` (the per-frame, priority-averaged axis update queue).
- Registration: `detail::RegisterRoboticsModules()` (servo_register.cpp) from `RegisterBuiltinModules`.

### Gate

- Reference: `tools/wp52/servo_reference.py` -> `tests/data/wp52_reference.json` (10 MB, fixed seeds; regenerate with
  `python -I tools/wp52/servo_reference.py > tests/data/wp52_reference.json`, byte-identical). Written from the C# only, before the port, no shared code: its own
  object model (a dict of KSPFields, handler lists, one hand-written state machine per class), the Mono float rule (`st()` at the C# stores).
  Its inputs are replayed by the C++ tests.
- Servos: 92 runs (26 hinge, 20 rotation servo, 22 piston, 24 rotor) x 120 fixed ticks, scripted coordinates with standing-still stretches (so the lock
  is accepted), random set / lock / unlock / motor / limit / brake / extend ops, PAW open or closed, auto-start on or off: per tick the rate-of-motion
  average, `currentFrameVelocity`, the double `rate`, `motorOutput`, the drive target, the joint drive spring / damper / force, limits, lock angle, mass and
  cost, drag-cube weights, `IsMoving`, the lock events: **all bit for bit (NaN == NaN, the sign of zero)**.
- Controller: 60 runs x 60 ticks (all four loop modes, direction toggles, play / stop events, action windows incl. the exact-end rule of Once, axis updates
  with multipliers 1 / 100 / length).
- Presets: 80 cases x 2 calls (cached reference, phase, soft-limit override, controller 0..1 range): every key (time, value, tangents) bit for bit; the up to
  two keys per curve that the C# derives from `AnimationCurve.Evaluate` (native) against the reference's double Hermite at a stated tolerance. The Python
  reproduces `FloatCurve(Keyframe[])` rejecting a key at an existing time (the synthetic start key and the first reference key share time 0 for whole-key phases).
- Joint: 72 `SetTargetRotationLocal` cases (6 axes x 12) against a double-precision quaternion algebra (<= 1e-5 per component; `Quaternion.LookRotation` is
  an UNVERIFIED native), the physical angle read back; 40 D6 drive parameter sets x 100 steps against the Python twin.
- Derived cases (labelled, expectations hand-derived from the cited C#): registration and every C# initialiser, lifecycle / OnSave / OnLoad, locks and
  their double events, power loss (the charge running out disengages, then locks), warp, `IsJointUnlocked` / `ServoArticulation` / the 2-cluster split,
  closed loops on the plant (hinge tracking lag = c / k * rate, settle, soft clamp; mirrored hinge; rotor spool-up to `rpmLimit` rpm measured from the Transform,
  brake, direction; piston ramp; rotation servo through 180 degrees), symmetric / mirrored decisions in Radial and Mirror modes, editor visualisation
  of the base, the rotor ratchet, power-loss braking of the rotor, slave transforms, attach node updates, controller bookkeeping (symmetry partner axes,
  transfer on delete, other-vessel cleanup, id changes), the manager's priority queue, persistence, the curve helpers (hand-computed keys), the quirks below.

### Findings kept from the C# (quirks)

- `ModuleRoboticServoPiston.ModifyLimits` looks up `Fields["TargetExtension"]` (capital T): no such field, its min / max update never runs.
- `ModuleRoboticController.SetSequencePositionNextKey` tests the ACTION times with `<` (like the previous-key search); `SequencePlay` / `SequenceStop` fire their
  event when the state did NOT change; `CycleLoopMode` fires the loop event a second time; `RemovePartAxis` / `RemovePartAction` call `RemoveAt(count)` once per
  same-vessel symmetry partner, so a part with two or more partners removes other rows (List.RemoveAt out of range throws; reproduced, tested for one partner only).
- `ControlledAxis.ClampPointValue(index)` accepts `index == length` (IndexOutOfRange).
- `BaseServo.GetModuleMass` reads `driveUnit`, refreshed only by `SetDriveUnit` (GetModuleCost, ModifyServo, GetInfo): stale (0) before.
- `HasEnoughResourcesToAutoStart` is false unless the input RESOURCE has a start-up handler: a servo whose cfg has none never restarts after a power loss;
  `IsResourceBelowShutOffLimit` without a shut-off handler is true while `currentAmount >= 0.01` of the first input.
- The hinge and the rotation servo read `servoJoint.xDrive` (the LINEAR drive) and write `angularXDrive`; the rotor does the same in XYAndZ mode.
- Mirrored hinges: `OnJointInit` sets the joint limits from the unmirrored soft range (the module's limits only match when `mirrorRotation` is false and
  `modelInitialAngle` 0); the plant (physical angle = minus the joint coordinate) therefore stops a mirrored hinge at 0.
- `OnPartMenuOpen` gates `UpdatePAWUI`, which writes `currentAngle` / `currentRPM`: with the PAW closed the hinge's "ignore tiny motion at the stops" test reads a stale
  `currentAngle` (reproduced; the gate runs PAW open and closed).

### Natives and seams (UNVERIFIED, no C# source exists)

- `ConfigurableJoint` property defaults (`maximumForce = float.MaxValue`, zero springs), the PhysX D6 drive law of `HeadlessServoPlant`, and the sign convention
  between `targetRotation` / `targetPosition` and the physical coordinate (derived from the algebra of SetTargetRotationInternal, `servo_joint.cpp`).
- `Quaternion.LookRotation` (WP-40's UNVERIFIED shim), `Quaternion.ToAngleAxis` (the rotor's free-spin ratchet), `Quaternion.eulerAngles` of the moving
  transform (`currentTransformAngle`; the gate bypasses it with `angleSource`), `Matrix4x4.inverse` (double Gauss-Jordan rounded to float), `AnimationCurve.MoveKey`
  (the curve helpers keep key order, tangents as given), the Transform hierarchy (`ServoNode`: the host fills it from the `.mu` hierarchy, not in the repo).
- `TimeWarp::CurrentRateIndex()` is 1 without a TimeWarp instance (kspcore's default), which reads as "physics warp" in the servo drive branches: tests install one.
- Module order of `FixedUpdate` / `Update` / `OnUpdate` between the servo and the part module hooks is the host's (as WP-29b R5); the Unity messages are explicit calls.

### Not ported (UI / PAW / audio / FX / editor GUI)

`UpdatePAWUI`'s control visibility and every `UI_FloatRange` / `UI_MinMaxRange` / `UI_Cycle` limit (min, max, step, `SetSceneVisibility`), the part-action-window
items, `GetInfo` / `GetModuleDisplayName` text, `Localizer` string caches (`CacheLocalStrings`), `RoboticControllerWindow*` (the editor window, rows, axis graph),
`CurvePanel*`, `AxisLimitLine`, `ModuleRobotArmScanner` (a ModuleDeployablePart with the arm-scan FX: separate package) and its `RobotArmFX`, the editor re-parenting of
child GameObjects (`BaseServo.SetChildParentTransform`), `Debug.Log`, the servo audio / animation clips. `SerenityUtils` assets are WP-53's seam.

### Residual risks

- The servo behaviour in motion has no game truth: only the formulas that the C# computes in managed float32 are bit-gated; PhysX's response is replaced by the documented
  plant. A capture of one hinge, one piston and one rotor (target steps, `ConfigurableJoint` drives, Transform angle per fixed tick) would validate the plant's sign
  conventions and the lag model.
- The synthetic MODULE fixtures use the C# defaults; real part cfg values (servoMotorSize, traverse limits, resource rates, the model's transform names) are not available.
- The Python reference was written from the same C# by the same author as the port; the quirks list above is where a reading error would hide (independent re-derivation
  of the UpdateCurrentExtension matrix path, CheckSymmetry's reflection and the preset key generation is what the gate covers).

- Windows MSVC RelWithDebInfo, fresh (`core/build` deleted, `run_tests.ps1 -Fresh`, `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=6`): configure 3.9 s, build 271.5 s, ctest 145.2 s,
  **48 / 48 pass** (before: 47 + the new `robotics` entry; `unit.random_order.11 / .27 / .42` and the eight `unit.shard.N` included); no compiler warning in any WP-52 file.
  The WP-52 cases alone: 34 / 34, 18,687 assertions (404,308 servo + 47,854 controller + 8,208 preset reference comparisons inside them).
- `check_cites.py` exact: 289 citations over the WP-52 sources, 0 mismatches (`ServoFixedUpdate` is aliased to `OnFixedUpdate` in the checker); `tools/wp55/check_cites.py` 165 / 0.
- The reference JSON regenerates byte-identically (`python -I core/tools/wp52/servo_reference.py`, fixed seeds, sha256 prefix 6e9ebec66176a6e9).
- Mutation check: the rotor spool step on `Time.deltaTime`, or a scaled PingPong fold, fails the scripted servo / controller gates at the first affected scenario.
- Linux was not run locally (WSL clang / gcc, README "Sanitizer run"); CI covers it.

## WP-20e: contact, landing and water (branch `wp20e`, from origin/main cd5e4df4; main `ccf3ffc9` (WP-mucol, WP-52) and `0d9fd73c` (WP-29c) merged)

State: done for the engine-agnostic part. Scope = PHYSICS-SPIKE.md section 7 row WP-20e on the WP-20b binding, the WP-19b bubble and the WP-20d
tick: what KSP did through Unity's collision callbacks, its per-part MonoBehaviours (PartBuoyancy, CollisionEnhancer) and its raycasts. The
contacts Jolt finds become Part.OnCollisionEnter / Stay / Exit with a `Collision` record; the Part.cs collision code decides ground contact,
Landed / Splashed / landedAt, the situation and the crash tolerance; the landed RB anchor ends the pad rocking; PartBuoyancy floats parts in the
ocean; CollisionEnhancer catches fast parts before they tunnel; WP-12b's terrain colliders are hosted per celestial body in the bubble's frame.
SAS / Vessel.FeedInputFeed is NOT wired (too large for this package, see Seams): `PhysicsBubble::inputFeed` is the labelled slot. **Gates**: an
independent Python reference (`tools/wp20e/contact_reference.py`, no kspcore code) for every decision and float statement ported (0 ULP / exact),
and scenarios against analytic values and KSP's own rules (no golden or capture covers contacts). Every existing gate is unchanged
(`harness/compare/tolerances.json`, `tests/tolerances_capture.json` untouched); the WP-20b / 19b / 20c / 20d suites pass with the contact host on
in every bubble (their numbers did not move: GameSettings' anchor values are 0 in those fixtures, so no anchor forms there).

### Exact / approximate / changed

| choice | class | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Part / Vessel / PartBuoyancy / CollisionEnhancer statements and decisions | exact | the reference above (Mono float rule) |
| Collision.relativeVelocity | approximate | the two clusters' velocities at the parts' centres of mass from Jolt's pre-solve (post-force) state with the post-step lever arms; PhysX reports its own pre-solver velocities |
| contact offset 0.01 m | approximate | Unity's Physics.defaultContactOffset; KSP's DynamicsManager asset is not extracted |
| dispatch order | changed | PhysX's report order is not observable: new contacts, kept ones, then lost ones, each sorted (a part sliding from one quad to the next never reads as airborne) |
| RB anchor | reduced model | a fixed-to-world weld of the root's cluster; joint.currentForce = the cluster's support force (Jolt carries the support in contacts, PhysX in the joint: the C# reads the joint's force); the cluster's motion is stopped when the anchor forms (else Jolt's anchor takes the quasi-static impulse and the WP-20c loads of L2-AS spike) |
| rb.drag | approximate | PhysX's per-step damping as a per-part force, first order in dt |
| CollisionEnhancer's world shift | reduced model | FloatingOrigin.Offset = the bubble's ShiftWorld plus the frame drift of the tick |
| PartBuoyancy's Invoke timer | approximate | Unity's Invoke fires between frames; here at the next FixedUpdate past its time |
| physicsless / asteroid / fairing collider branches of CheckCollision, wheel damage | seam | they compare model colliders the proxies do not have (`PartContactEnvironment`) |
| PhysicMaterial "Ground", KSC collider tags | FIXTURE | not extracted (WP-12b's open item; the tests label them) |
| ROC branch (Breaking Ground) | not ported | DLC |

| Collider.ClosestPoint (getLowestPoint) | exact / approximate | box, sphere, capsule proxies exact; a convex hull (WP-mucol's mesh colliders): the hull vertex furthest towards the measure point, which is 1,000 m away (Vessel.cs:2587): the same height as the true closest point to within extent^2 / 1,000 m |
| CheckGroundCollision's PQS surface height | seam | `Vessel::env.pqsSurfaceHeight`, unset = the body radius |
| several world steps per FixedUpdate (WP-29c's physics-warp substeps) | changed | Unity runs one PhysX simulate per FixedUpdate (KSP's physics warp is one 0.08 s step); with substeps every step's Enter / Exit is dispatched in step order (an impact inside any substep runs HandleCollision), OnCollisionStay once per pair; the RB anchor's force and break check read the last substep |
| Unity Vector3 unary minus (`0f - x`) | noted | kspcore's `Vector3f` uses `-x`: differs only in the sign of zero; not changed here |

### Findings (a later implementer must know)

- **The pad rocking of WP-20b R2 is KSP's anchor's job**: KSP never lets a landed vessel rest on contacts for long; after 1.5 s still and
  landed it welds the vessel to the world (Vessel.cs:1105) and releases the weld at ignition, on a change of the force direction or on a downward
  force. With the anchor the three crafts rest at exactly zero speed.
- **`Vessel::env.timeSinceLevelLoad` defaults to 10 s (WP-19a)**: in a scene that does not advance it, Vessel.LateUpdate's bounce check
  (Vessel.cs:3061: once the level is 5 s old, UpdateLandedSplashed once) runs in the first frame, before any contact, and PRELAUNCH becomes
  LANDED. The WP-20e fixtures model the level clock (`ResetLevelClock`, `Tick` advances it by the frame time); the WP-19b / 20d fixtures are
  unchanged (their gates do not read the situation).
- The pre-solve velocity of a contact already has this step's gravity: the reported impact of a drop is the speed aimed at plus about g dt
  (0.196 m/s: 8.30 vs 8.1 m/s). KSP sees the same kind of number (PhysX's pre-solver velocity).
- Jolt's body-pair cache skips the contact callbacks of a pair whose relative pose did not change: the pair is still touching (Stay), as
  WP-20c's StaticContacts already handled.
- A part landing on another vessel takes that vessel's landedAt (LandedCollisionChecks' part branch), not the static's tag.

### Seams (named, with what a host or a later package does)

- **SAS / Vessel.FeedInputFeed (not wired)**: `PhysicsBubble::inputFeed` runs at FlightInputHandler.FixedUpdate's slot (seq 11, before the part
  modules); unset = nothing. Wiring needs a port of Vessel.FeedInputFeed (OnPreAutopilotUpdate, OnAutopilotUpdate: WP-24's VesselSAS is already
  connected there, OnPostAutopilotUpdate, OnFlyByWire, Part.propagateControlUpdate), WP-50's FlightInputHandler.FixedUpdate driven by the bubble
  (`FlightInputHandler`'s `feedInputFeed` hook), and ModuleGimbal actuation in WP-20d's module slot with the gimbal transform chains from the model
  reader (today the thrust transforms stay at the neutral pose). Reaction-wheel torque already flows. That is what lets the WP-20d ascent gate go past
  Mach 1 / 5 km.
- KSC / launch-site colliders and their tags (LaunchPad, Runway ...): WP-mucol's scenery collider loader builds their static bodies, but the data is
  not extracted yet (WP-mucol "Blocker" 2); a host registers each body's key with its GameObject's tag / name through
  `ContactHost::RegisterStatic` (unregistered statics read as untagged terrain).
- PhysicMaterial "Ground" friction / bounce: FIXTURE (WP-12b).
- Part colliders: WP-mucol's real .mu colliders reach the contact host through `VesselPhysicsOptions::colliders` (one contact pair per sub-shape,
  getLowestPoint over every shape kind); the stock-part sweep is WP-mucol's open item. Still seams: CheckCollision's asteroid / fairing branches
  (they compare the touching collider with the part's own model colliders by identity), the colliders' layer / tag (every proxy reads as layer 0).
- Wheels (WP-29c): ModuleWheelBase's ground contact goes through its own WheelCollider; wheel damage is a `PartContactEnvironment` hook.
- FX: `PartContactEnvironment::explodeFx`, `ContactHost::splashFx` (FXMonger), recorded only.

Textual conflicts only in STATUS.md (rows / sections; WP-mucol took row 55, so this package is row 58). `physics_world`, `vessel_physics`,
the CMake lists merged cleanly. WP-mucol's `ColliderProxy` kinds (sphere, capsule, convex hull) reach the contact host's getLowestPoint hook,

the contact events need no change (they are per sub-shape, whatever its shape). With the default proxies (drag-cube boxes) every WP-20e number
above is unchanged after the merge.

### Merge with main (`0d9fd73c`: WP-29c wheels)

- Conflicts: `PhysicsBubble::PhysicsStep` (WP-29c's `physicsStep` override, then the contact host after it), the CMake source lists and the
  docs (both sides kept; STATUS rows 56 WP-29c, 57 WP-52, 58 WP-20e).
- **Substeps**: WheelPhysicsHost::PhysicsStep steps the world `ceil(dt / 0.02)` times per FixedUpdate in physics warp; the contact host read
  `PhysicsWorld::ContactEvents()`, the LAST step's only, so a contact that began in an earlier substep never sent OnCollisionEnter (no crash
  check, no landing). `PhysicsWorld` now also keeps a log of every step's events until `TakeContactEventLog()`; the contact host dispatches
  them step by step (Enter / Stay / Exit each step, OnCollisionStay once per FixedUpdate and pair). One step per FixedUpdate dispatches
  exactly as before (every WP-20e number unchanged). New cases: `contact event log`, `physics-warp substeps` (above).
- **WP-29c's rover fixture**: its flat ground is at Kerbin's sea level (no PQS), where KSP's PartBuoyancy finds the wheels below the water line
  (depth -0.07 to -0.23 m at the wheel centres, maxDepth +0.09 to +0.21 m): with the contact host on, the wheels floated with water drag 2
  (BuoyancyWaterDragSlow), the vessel read Splashed and 3 of 13 WP-29c cases failed (rest forces 7 % short of the weight, drive -26 % at 10 s).
  `RoverScene` now turns the PartBuoyancy slot off (`tests/vessel_wheels_fixture.hpp`, commented); every WP-29c case passes. With the rest of the
  contact host on, the WP-29c numbers are unchanged to the digits STATUS shows (drive 19.4188 / 28.3923 m/s, brake 7.38 / 8.30 m, steer, warp
  with substeps) except the braked rest drift (Prospector 0.60 mm, was 0.26; Bug-E 0.34 mm, unchanged; gate 5 mm) and the chaotic 4x runs
  without substeps (Prospector 2.19 m, was 2.51; Bug-E 5.34 m, was 12.5; gate > 0.1 m). The wheel parts are in Vessel.GroundContacts through
  ModuleWheelBase, so Vessel.VesselAnchorExceptions keeps a rover from anchoring (Vessel.cs:1111-1121), as in KSP.
- **Crash damage in the rover cases**: `unit.random_order.27` / `.42` crashed (SIGSEGV) in `WP-29c physics warp`: after an earlier WP-50
  InputFixture case (it runs GameSettings.SetDefaultValues; bisected over the 63 preceding cases) the 4x drive WITHOUT substeps (KSP's single
  0.08 s step) bounced the Prospector's root decoupler onto the ground at 7.1 m/s, Part.HandleCollision exploded it (KSP's crash tolerance:
  a faithful outcome, and one more reason for WP-29c's substeps), the vessel died and the test's `Healthy()` dereferenced the missing
  binding. The library did not crash (the tick finished; traced). `RoverScene` sets CheatOptions.NoCrashDamage
  (`PartContactEnvironment::noCrashDamage`) since those cases measure the wheels, and `Healthy()` returns false once the vessel has no rigid
  bodies. Default-order numbers unchanged (nothing exploded there).

### Risks

- R1: impacts load the WP-20c joints as one-step spikes (no compliance): PhysProf-S touching down at 6 m/s reaches 0.98 of a sub-joint's
  capacity although its Mainsail survives the contact (crashTolerance 7). KSP's joints would flex; a harder touchdown would break a joint here that
  KSP keeps. A compliance term in the load model (or an impact filter) is the fix.
- R2: Collision.relativeVelocity is not PhysX's number bit for bit (pre-solve velocities of a different solver): impacts near a crashTolerance can
  decide differently from KSP by a few cm/s. The decision itself is KSP's (reference).
- R3: no in-game capture of contacts, landing or buoyancy exists: the scenarios are analytic or KSP-rule checks (a capture of a drop / splashdown
  would close it).
- R4: the anchor zeroes the cluster's velocity when it forms; KSP's FixedJoint removes it through the joint solve. The rule anchors only a vessel
  slower than sqrt(VESSEL_ANCHOR_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD) = 0.22 m/s (GameSettings.cs:1121), so the jump is below that; on the pad it is ~1e-9 m/s.

## WP-12c: KSC / launch-site scenery colliders and ground PhysicMaterials from the game's assets (branch `wp12c`, from main `51530d89`, main `e43c8576` merged)

State: done for the engine-agnostic part. The scenery colliders of every PQSCity / PQSCity2 of the stock game (59 cities: the KSC with all facility levels and destruction states, the island airfield, the four stock mobile launch sites with their set dressings, KSC2, the Mun / Kerbin / Duna ... monuments), the PhysicMaterials (terrain "Ground", `Physics.defaultMaterial`), the GameObject layer / tag / CrashObjectName data of the contact records and the PSystemSetup launch-site / facility table are extracted from `KSP_x64_Data` with UnityPy, checked against the assets by a second, independent extraction, and hosted in the physics bubble through `ContactHost::RegisterStatic`. Every existing gate is unchanged (49 / 49 ctest; the PhysX material combine is opt-in per world).

### What was extracted (all from `decompiled/KSP-dev/KSP_x64_Data`, UnityPy 1.25.4, Unity 2019.4.18f1; origin file + pathID recorded per object, sha256 of every asset file in the JSON `source.files`)

| output | content | size |
|---|---|---|
| `data/scenery/scenery_colliders.json` (schema `kspcore-scenery-colliders/2`) | 59 cities, 4,463 GameObjects (path, parent, `src` file + pathID, activeSelf, layer, tag name, local TRS as float32, CrashObjectName, PositionMobileLaunchPad, level group / level), 2,585 colliders (2,001 mesh, rest box / sphere / capsule; trigger and enabled flags), PQSCity.lod / PQSCity2.objects, 75 DestructibleBuilding records at the KSC, PhysicMaterials, per-body terrain material, PhysicsManager defaults, TagManager tags, `PSystemSetup.stocklaunchsites` + `facilities` | 2.1 MB |
| `data/scenery/scenery_meshes.bin` | 712 Mesh assets of the MeshColliders (float32 xyz, uint32 triangle indices), each with origin file / pathID and the sha256 of its bytes in the JSON | 16.9 MB |
| `tests/data/wp12c_extraction_digest.json` | sha256 of both files and what `tools/wp12c/verify_scenery_extraction.py` verified against the game | |
| `tests/data/wp12c_reference.json` | output of `tools/wp12c/scenery_reference.py` (below) | 0.7 MB |

The tree is what the game runs with, not the raw prefab: `NestedPrefabSpawner` ("Kerbin/KSC/SpaceCenter" is a spawner; the KSC buildings are the prefab sharedassets9 pathID 5726, instantiated in its place with the target's TRS / name and `setLayersAndTagsRecursive`, NestedPrefabSpawner.cs:20 / :60) and `UpgradeableObject` (each of the 19 facility / slave groups has 2 or 3 level prefabs replacing the "Facility" transform, UpgradeableObject.cs:9; ALL levels are in the data with `levelGroup` / `level`; the host chooses with `SceneryLevels`: level 0 = a fresh career, highest = sandbox) are replayed by the extractor. 808 objects get their tag from a spawner with `setTags` (that is how the pad tanks become "LaunchPad", the building sections "KSC_Tracking_Station_Hub" ...). Stock launch sites without DLC: KSC LaunchPad + Runway (facilities), `Island_Airfield`, `Crater_` / `MahiMahi_` / `Cove_` / `GlacierLake_Launch_Site` (PQSCity2 in the PQS prefab, bundle "stock"; their set-dressing prefabs `additionalprefabPaths` are `sharedassets0` GameObjects and extracted as extra cities "Kerbin/<name>" with their PQSCity2 `placement` fields). `Woomerang_Launch_Site`, `Desert_Airfield`, `Desert_Launch_Site` are bundle `makinghistory_assets` (DLC, not installed): in the launch-site table, no scenery.

### Materials (replaces the WP-12b / WP-mucol / WP-20e FIXTURE 0.6)

| material | origin | dynamic / static friction | bounciness | friction / bounce combine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Ground" | sharedassets9 PhysicMaterial 2499; `PQSMod_QuadMeshColliders.physicsMaterial` of Kerbin, Minmus, Moho, Eve, Laythe, Dres (Mun, Duna, Ike, Vall, Bop, Tylo, Gilly, Pol, Eeloo: none) | 0.9 / 0.9 | 0 | Maximum / Minimum |
| "Metal" = `Physics.defaultMaterial` | globalgamemanagers PhysicsManager `m_DefaultMaterial` (pathID 3363) | 0.25 / 0.25 | 0 | Maximum / Minimum |

No stock scenery collider carries a material of its own, and no stock part has `ModulePhysicMaterial`: every part collider, every KSC collider and every Ground-less terrain therefore has "Metal" (Unity applies `Physics.defaultMaterial` to colliders without one). Part vs Ground = max(0.25, 0.9) = 0.9; part vs KSC = 0.25; part vs part = 0.25. Also recorded: `Physics.bounceThreshold` 0.2, `defaultContactOffset` 0.01.

`PhysicsWorldConfig::physxMaterials` (+ `defaultMaterial`, `minVelocityForRestitution`) combines a contact pair as PhysX does (PxsMaterialCombiner: the combine mode of higher priority wins, Average < Minimum < Multiply < Maximum; Jolt has one friction per contact: the dynamic value is used, stock static == dynamic) from `PhysicMaterialDesc` carried by `ShapeDesc::material` (null = world default) and `AddStaticMesh(..., material)`; implemented with a `PhysicsMaterial` subclass on the Jolt shapes and `PhysicsSystem::SetCombineFriction / Restitution`. `SceneryColliders::ApplyTo(cfg)` fills it from the data; `TerrainCollidersOptions::material` (`SceneryColliders::TerrainMaterialDesc(body)`) gives the PQ quads their Ground. OFF by default (Jolt's rule sqrt(f1 f2), the bodies' friction), so WP-20b/c/d/e, WP-29c and the other existing numbers did not move; a flight host turns it on with `ApplyTo`. UNVERIFIED against a capture: PhysX also applies the static friction coefficient for sticking contacts and Unity's `Physics.bounceThreshold`; Jolt's `mMinVelocityForRestitution` stands in for the latter.

### Hosting API (documented for WP-29d and the flight host)

```
SceneryColliders doc = LoadSceneryColliders(".../core/data/scenery/scenery_colliders.json");   // reads scenery_meshes.bin next to it
PhysicsWorldConfig cfg; doc.ApplyTo(cfg);                                                       // game materials (optional)
SceneryCityHost ksc(bubble, *doc.Find("Kerbin/KSC"), keyBase, levels);   // keys keyBase + object << 16 + collider
ksc.PlaceOnBody(kerbin, Vector3d(pqsCity.localPosition), QuaternionD(pqsCity.localRotation));   // WP-42 PQSCity::Orientate output
ksc.ActivateAll();    // or ksc.Update(targetInPhysicsFrame) = PQSCity.OnUpdateFinished; Deactivate() = OnSphereInactive
```

`SceneryCityHost` (`include/ksp/physics/scenery_host.hpp`) wraps `PQSCityColliders` / `PQSCity2Colliders` (WP-12b) over the real objects: `children` and `lod[].objects` are expanded to their subtrees honouring activeSelf (`SceneryActiveSubtree`), the objects no callback switches are active from the start (`SceneryInitiallyActive`: the root; for a PQSCity2 everything outside its LOD subtrees), non-selected facility levels are never placed, trigger and disabled colliders are dropped. Every placed collider is registered with `ContactHost::RegisterStatic(key, {layer, tag, name, crashObjectName, isMobileLaunchPad})`, so `Part.OnCollisionEnter` sees `c.gameObject.layer == 15` and `c.gameObject.tag` ("LaunchPad", "Runway", "KSC_Runway_09" ...) and `Vessel.SetLandedAt(tag)` (Part.cs:3417 LandedCollisionChecks, ported in WP-20e) names the site. `ContactHost::RefreshTerrain` (frame changes, physics-origin rebases) re-places the city (`AddRefreshHook`). Wheels: `WheelPhysicsHost` now answers `describeCollider` for registered scenery (layer, tag, CrashObjectName) instead of a single untagged terrain collider, so `ModuleWheelBase.LandingDetectionUpdate` (ModuleWheelBase.cs:473) sets `landedAt` from a wheel ray's hit. `SetBuildingDestroyed(index, bool)` applies `CollapsibleObject.SetDestroyed` (collapse subtree off / replacement on) immediately; the collapse animation and the DestructibleBuilding state machine stay WP-42's. For WP-29d (runway): the runway is `Kerbin/KSC` objects tagged `Runway` / `KSC_Runway_*` (level group "SpaceCenter/Runway", SpawnPoint transforms `.../Runway/Facility/End09/SpawnPoint`, `End27`).

CheckCollision (Part.cs:3539) itself has no tag branch (the asteroid / fairing branches compare model colliders); the tag-dependent Part code is LandedCollisionChecks (:3417), OnCollisionEnter's CrashObjectName / ROC branch (:3401-3413) and CheckOtherGroundContact, all of which now receive real tags / layers / names from the registry.

### Exclusions, unverified, deferred

- Making History scenery (Woomerang, Desert Airfield / Launch Site, Larkes, ground objects): DLC not installed; only the table rows.
- 79 of 2,585 colliders are triggers or disabled (dropped by the loader as no contact response); 7 MeshColliders have no mesh assigned in the game (left out, warned in `warnings`).
- Mesh colliders are static triangle meshes whatever the convex flag (the flag is kept); PhysX would treat a convex-flagged mesh as its hull. Wheel-collider and trigger objects (ladders, PadFXReceiver) are not colliders in the bubble.
- Collider transforms use lossyScale as Unity (no shear); mesh vertices go through the same float chain as part colliders, UNVERIFIED against a Unity `Collider.bounds` capture.
- Facility level at run time (`ScenarioUpgradeableFacilities`) and the destruction state machine are not wired: the host takes `SceneryLevels`; `SetBuildingDestroyed` is immediate.
- The pad scenario places the craft on the pad collider without the VAB launch sequence (WP-42 `LaunchSiteFacility` + ShipConstruction's `PutShipToGround` offset) and without the PQS terrain under it; the KSC pad's `PQSMod_FlattenArea` ground vs the pad collider is not compared.
- `PhysicsWorldConfig::physxMaterials` is off by default; turning it on for the flight bubble changes the friction of every contact (part vs terrain 0.6 -> 0.9, part vs part 0.6 -> 0.25) and is the host's decision (the WP-20b/e/29c numbers would have to be re-measured). Static vs dynamic friction and PhysX's bounce threshold not modelled.
- No in-game capture of a pad settle / landing exists; the scenarios are analytic / reference-gated, not capture gates.
- The extraction needs the game; re-run: `harness/tools-cache/venv/Scripts/python.exe -I core/tools/mucollider/extract_scenery_colliders.py <KSP_x64_Data> harness/lib core/data/terrain/pqs_prefab.json core/data/scenery`, then `verify_scenery_extraction.py ... --report core/tests/data/wp12c_extraction_digest.json`, then `python -I core/tools/wp12c/scenery_reference.py core/data/scenery core/tests/data/wp12c_reference.json`. Finding on the way: the UnityPy type-tree generator types a `string[]` field as one string (PSystemSetup.LaunchSite.additionalprefabPaths); the extractor patches such nodes to vectors.

## WP-52b: the joint drive backend of the servos on the reduced Jolt model (branch `wp52b`, from main `51530d89`; main `e43c8576` merged)

State: done for the engine-agnostic part. Scope = NEXT-STEPS.md "WP-52 robotics", follow-up 1: the servos wrote `ConfigurableJointData` (WP-52) and
the reduced rigid-body model had only fixed constraints. Now a servo has its own servo body (Part.servoRb), the servo's moving side is a cluster of its
own, and a Jolt hinge / slider with a drive motor reads the joint data every physics step and moves the moving transform after it:
`HeadlessServoPlant` is no longer in the loop (it stays as the reference plant of the gate). **Gates**: an independent Python reference of the drive
law (`tools/wp52b/drive_reference.py`, no kspcore code), closed loops of the four servo kinds on a real two-part craft against the reference plant with
the same effective inertia and against closed forms, the structural loads across the servo, a physics-bubble scenario with the FlightIntegrator, and
determinism at 1 / 4 threads. **No capture of a servo exists** (the SquadExpansion parts are not installed): the sign conventions (servo_joint.cpp's
derivation), the PhysX drive law and its limit / limit-spring behaviour stay **UNVERIFIED**; every servo MODULE value in the tests is a labelled

### What KSP does (the spec)

- BaseServo.CreateServoRigidbody (Expansions/Serenity/BaseServo.cs:1196): a second Rigidbody on the moving transform, `part.servoRb`; each servo's
  OnJointInit (ModuleRoboticServoHinge.cs:337 and the other three) adds a ConfigurableJoint to the moving GameObject (one axis free / limited, five
  locked), PostStartInitJoint connects it to `part.Rigidbody` (BaseServo.cs:1158). The parts on the servo's moving nodes are jointed to the servo
  body (AttachServoRigidBody / NodeRigidBody, BaseServo.cs:1602 / :1627, through PartJoint.SetupJoint).
- FlightIntegrator.UpdateMassStats (FlightIntegrator.cs:476-480): with a servoRb, `rb.mass = servoRb.mass = num2 / 2f`; Part.ValidateInertiaTensor
  (Part.cs:4263-4271): both get `inertiaTensor * Max(1, mass)`; FlightIntegrator.Integrate (:728-731): `servoRb.AddForce(integrationAccel,
  Acceleration)`; UpdateAerodynamics (:2268-2281, :2366-2369): `servoRb.angularDrag = rb.angularDrag`; PartBuoyancy (:550-555, :571-586) the same in water.
- The drive: positionSpring k, positionDamper c, maximumForce F and the targets (targetRotation / targetPosition / targetAngularVelocity), written by
  ModuleRoboticServoHinge.cs:442-469, ModuleRoboticRotationServo.cs:445-480, ModuleRoboticServoPiston.cs:396-431, ModuleRoboticServoRotor.cs:465-481 /
  :637-648; PhysX integrates F = k (xt - x) + c (vt - v), |F| <= F, implicitly (native: UNVERIFIED).

| articulated constraints | `physics/physics_world.hpp`, `src/physics/physics_world.cpp` | `CreateArticulatedConstraint(a, b, desc)`: a Jolt HingeConstraint / SliderConstraint whose zero is the caller's coordinate zero (the bodies read `coordinate0` at creation); `SetArticulatedDrive`: the motor in `PositionAndVelocity` mode with a `StiffnessAndDamping` spring (k, c), the torque / force limit, limits and limit springs (soft when spring > 0); `ArticulatedCoordinate` / `ArticulatedRate`; `GetConstraintImpulse` returns the world impulse on b (the hinge's two-row rotation lambdas rebuilt in the basis HingeRotationConstraintPart derived from the set-up rotations, which Step records); per-joint solver iterations (`velocitySteps`, Jolt's per-constraint override) |

### Gate, the drive law (`tests/test_servo_backend.cpp`, 3 cases; `tools/wp52b/drive_reference.py` -> `tests/data/wp52b_reference.json`, seed 5252)

| case | what | result |
|---|---|---|
| coordinate and locks | a hinge / slider reads its creation coordinate (0, 0.7, -2.5); a +axis spin reads as a positive rate; pushes across the axis are held | to 1e-6; locked rates < 1e-3 rad/s, pivot drift < 1 mm |
| **drive law** | the 28 reference cases (12 position drives, 6 MoveTowards ramps, 6 torque-limited velocity drives = the rotor, 4 holds against a load) as hinge and as slider on a body with the axis through its centre of mass (50 runs of 200-400 steps) against the Python implicit D6 law v1 = (v0 + dt/I (k (xt - x0) + c vt + L)) / (1 + dt/I (c + dt k)) with the force clamp | worst relative \|dx\| **1.6e-5**, \|dv\| **4.9e-5** (Jolt's float velocities; gate 2e-4); the analytic markers: ramp lag c / k * rate (5 %), torque-limited spool time I vt / F (3 %), hold offset L / k (0.1 %) |
| solver characterisation | a velocity drive on a body hinged 2.4 m from its centre of mass | the steady rate falls short by 0.0028 rad/s of 3.14 (predicted m r^2 w (1 - cos w dt) / (c dt) = 0.0032; gate 20 %); 0 without the arm (Findings) |

Jolt's PositionAndVelocity motor solves J v + s lambda + b = 0 with s = 1 / (dt (c + dt k)), b = -vt + dt k s C: the implicit law above with the target
extrapolated by vt dt, i.e. the same law for the hinge / rotation servo / piston (vt = 0) and different by k dt vt for the rotor (k = 1e-10: nil).

### Findings (a later implementer must know)

- **A velocity-level solver dissipates rotation about an off-centre pivot**: the first-order step moves the centre of mass along the old tangent and
  the point constraint removes the radial part, so the tangential speed loses (1 - cos(w dt)) per step. A rotor turning an 18 t tank 2.4 m off its
  axis at 3 rad/s loses ~30 kN m (characterised in `test_servo_backend.cpp`); PhysX in KSP solves at the same level, so KSP's servos see the same kind
  of loss (magnitude UNVERIFIED). The rotor scenario therefore spins the tank about its own axis.
- **A light body welded to the world between a heavy arm and the anchor converges badly** (mass ratio 72:1: the halved probe core under the 18 t
  tank): the plant comparisons hold because the arm is slow; a fast rotor on such a base overshot its rate by 0.16 % at any iteration count. Real
  craft put servos between comparable masses; the RB anchor of a landed vessel (WP-20e) is such a weld.
- A servo test fixture must install the resource host BEFORE the servo module is added (`AddServo` / OnStart raise a NullReference otherwise).

### UNVERIFIED (no capture)

The sign convention between targetRotation / targetPosition / targetAngularVelocity and the physical coordinate (servo_joint.cpp's derivation, now
also the orientation of the backend's hinge / slider: + coordinate = the servo body turned about / moved along +GetMainAxis() in the joint parent's
frame), PhysX's D6 drive law and its limit / limit-spring behaviour, the Unity ConfigurableJoint defaults. A capture of one hinge, one piston and one
rotor (target steps, the ConfigurableJoint drive values, the Transform angle / position per fixed tick, servoRb.velocity) closes them.

How far it holds and why it diverges: M2 holds to the end of C10's flight (90 s, 36.7 km) at 0.1 %; L2-AS holds to its apex (fuel out, 11.5 km).
PhysProf-S is aerodynamically unstable from Mach ~0.9 (WP-20d finding): KSP's own S tumbled with SAS on (AoA 0.6 deg at Mach 1,
172.7 deg at 2.5 km) and ours does too (57.7 deg at 2.5 km): the tumble is a divergence of a small attitude error, so its course is not
reproducible and S is gated to Mach 1 (+1.40 % altitude there, the closest state to the 1.5 % tolerance; the transonic drag rise makes the altitude
at Mach 1 the most sensitive quantity of the three crafts). With a partial lifecycle (ModulesOnStart without the jettison's first LateUpdate,
which leaves the Mainsail's cube weights at zero) the same ascents differed by up to 1.4 % (M2 at 20 km) and 4.8 % (L2-AS at 10 km), and the
frame intervals by up to 3.2 %: the cube weights, not SAS, were the largest remaining error of the ascent.

| ModuleGimbal.FixedUpdate (one transform) | 5.25 us | **0.67 us** |

### Findings (a later implementer must know)

- **The module lifecycle sets the drag-cube weights KSP flies with.** ModulePartVariants.OnStart (RefreshVariant -> SetCubes) and the first
  ModuleJettison.LateUpdate (SetupJettisonState -> SetFairingDragCube) choose a part's cube; without them the default weights stay (24 of M2's 153
  parts, 72 of L2-AS's 457). WP-20d's ascent matched C10 to ~1 % with the wrong weights only up to 5 km; with the right ones M2 matches at 0.1 % to
  36.7 km. A host must run the module lifecycle before the first flight tick.
- **A probe's SAS needs Part.Start + Part.Update**: ModuleSAS.OnStart registers its service level with the part's PartValues, Part.Start sets
  overrideSkillUpdate (:1915), and Part.Update refreshes the PartValues (:4328) that VesselValues.AutopilotSASSkill folds; without them
  CanEngageSAS is false ("no operational SAS Modules") and the SAS action group switches itself off.
- **Windows: `ksp::dotnet::NativeSinf / NativeCosf / NativePowf` called getenv on every call** (the KSPCORE_LIBM_PORTABLE switch): 1.1 us per call,
  half of ModuleGimbal.FixedUpdate. Read once now; every caller of the Unity native float trig benefits (AngleAxis 330x faster).
- `ModuleGimbal.GetPotentialTorque` (WP-23) reads the gimbal transform's CURRENT (actuated) pose and the vessel's CoM: the transform must be on its
  part's post-step pose when VesselSAS sums the torque in FeedInputFeed.
- The LV-T45 v1 (liquidEngine2) gimbals its thrustTransform itself (gimbalTransformName = thrustTransform); the Mainsail gimbals `gimbal`, the
  thrust transform's parent (its thrust point moves 0.57 m x sin(angle) laterally with the gimbal).

### Risks

- R1: the actuated transform composition is not verified against Unity's native hierarchy (a capture of a gimbaled thrust transform's world pose
  would close it; the neutral pose is bit for bit WP-17b's).
- R2: VesselSAS is gated against KSP only through the C10 trajectory (no per-tick SAS capture, WP-24's "Needed in-game captures" 2).
- R3: the timings were taken while other agents built on the same laptop.

Circularity check: the Python reference reads the recorded INPUT kinematics of each tick (the state before the module ran) and recomputes the OUTPUT forces / deflections; no input is recovered from the output it checks. The rest / roll / braking gates compare against the weight, the engine's thrust impulse and v^2 / (2 x 2 g), none derived from the checked value. The lift-off prediction uses the reference's lift (not the simulation's) with the recorded thrust and weight.

### Exclusions (what the aircraft gates do not cover)

- The fuselage / body lift and drag (drag cubes) and the gear's contribution are not in the reference's vertical balance (only the lifting and control surfaces, the thrust and the weight are): this is why the lift-off and climb brackets are 5 %, not tighter.
- The robotic rotor-blade (`displaceVelocity`) branches of the control surface are the robotics package's.
- The 3 crafts of other mods do not load; the other 21 loaded crafts are assembled, not flown. Only the Aeris 3A is flown.

### Finding: the VTOL "attitude jump" of WP-29d is the gear-bay deployment pose, not a vessel rotation

WP-29d reported that `Rocket-power VTOL` spawns with its wheel colliders rotating ~25 degrees in the first ticks while the cluster hardly rotates. Measured (`tests/test_wheel_gear.cpp`, 40 ticks, airborne and on the ground, 4 LY-01 bays): the vessel's rotation moves by 1.0e-6 deg airborne / 3.5e-3 deg on the ground (gate 0.05); the wheel colliders' part-space pose changes ONCE, between tick 0 and tick 1, by 5.0 deg and 0.077 m (all four bays), then by 0.015 deg airborne / 0 on the ground (gate 0.05). That step is the deployment pose (`ModuleWheelDeployment.OnStart` samples the Animation at the deployed state; the prefab model is posed stowed). So no reference-transform switch exists and the vessel does not jump; nothing in the model was changed. The "~25 degrees" of WP-29d is not reproduced by this measurement (5 deg at the collider axis); its measure was not recorded there, so the cause of that larger figure is not established.

### Exact / approximate / changed

- No new bit-exactness claim: the new surface code follows the Mono float rule and is gated against float64 by the reference (worst 2.4e-5 relative, tolerances 2e-4); no harness golden or capture gate involves it.
- Approximate: the scenario values above (labelled analytic / reference-gated); the tyre model and its rolling resistance are WP-29c's (UNVERIFIED, C11).
- Changed behaviour of existing code: with `Hooks::modelTransform` set, a control surface without a `ctrlSurface` transform does not deflect (`hasCtrlSurface` false); unset keeps the old behaviour (present). `PartModuleForces::intakes` (default true) adds the intake FixedUpdate to the module slot, which did not run in the tick before. All existing WP-20d / WP-20f gates pass unchanged.

### Deferred / UNVERIFIED

1. No capture of an aircraft flight (lift-off speed, climb rate, trim, rolling resistance, braking): needs the in-game profiling branch (capture C11 for the wheels, a new one for the aerodynamics); all aircraft numbers are analytic / reference-gated.
2. Body lift / drag of the fuselage and cargo-bay interactions in the flown scenarios: WP-20d's drag path runs, but nothing compares it to an aircraft measurement.
3. The 3 mod-part crafts, flying any craft other than the Aeris 3A, rotor-blade control surfaces.
4. Colliders that follow the suspension / wheel transforms (WP-29d finding 3) apply to the LY-01 bays too.
5. The cause of WP-29d's "~25 degrees" figure (see the finding above).

| flight scene start | `PhysicsBubble` with `PhysicsBubbleOptions{contactHost, resourceHost, vessel.colliders = MuPartColliders::Hook()}` and a `PhysicsWorldConfig` from `SceneryColliders::ApplyTo` (game PhysicMaterials); `Install` | FlightIntegrator, Krakensbane, FloatingOrigin, PartBuoyancy, CollisionEnhancer, the Vessel resource fields | installs the Vessel::env pack / unpack / physics seams, the FlightIntegratorHost, PartModuleForces, ContactHost, VesselResourceHost (each restores what it replaced) |
| flight scene start | `PartModuleForces::hooks` (model transforms: thrust transforms, gimbal chains), `PhysicsBubble::SetFlightInputHandler` | the part model hierarchy, FlightInputHandler | WP-20d / WP-20f; data: core/data/engine_thrust_transforms.json |
| flight scene start | `SceneryCityHost` per PQSCity (the KSC at the career / sandbox facility levels, `PQSCity::Orientate` pose), `ContactHost::HostTerrain` | PQSCity, PQS colliders | WP-12c / WP-12b; optional `WheelPhysicsHost`, `UseServoBackend` (WP-29c / WP-52b) |
| flight scene start | `PSystemSetup` with the facility table (`SceneryColliders::facilities`) and `space_center::SceneGraph::FindInPQS / FindChild` over `SceneryFindObject` + `SceneryObjectPoses`; `SetupFacilities` | PSystemSetup.cs:378 | the spawn transforms of the launch sites |
| launch | `FlightDriver` statics (StartWithNewLaunch: craft path, flag, manifest, launch site), `host.placeAtSpawn = FloatingOrigin::SetOffset`, `host.beginNewVessel` = the parts' `colliderBounds` (model reader) + `ShipConstruction::PutShipToGround(ship, spawn pose)` + `AssembleForLaunch`, then `setStartupNewVessel` | FlightDriver.cs:272-371 | StageManager.BeginFlight, the crew roster and the scene switch stay the host's |

### Findings (a later implementer must know)

- **The module start-up alone moved WP-20d's numbers** (the startModules = false build reproduces the baseline): a host that skips it flies the
  default drag-cube weights. The GameSettings defaults in every case moved no gated number (the WP-20e cases already set the anchor values).
- **KSP's launch puts the lowest collider bound on the spawn transform and then CheckGroundCollision moves the vessel by about a decimetre**
  (the top-level spawn transform is ~0.1 m above the pad surface under the Mainsail bell): KSP 0.101 m, ours 0.119 m; the 1.8 cm is not explained
  by the pad triangles (WP-12c: 1.2e-4 m) and is consistent with the float32 hierarchy above. The settled root is 1.08 cm below KSP's.
- PutShipToGround's lowest point with the real Mainsail hull reproduces KSP's log text exactly (`-6.869718`), so ShipConstruction's float path, the
  craft's editor pose and the WP-mucol collider data agree with the game.
- GameSettings is a singleton with an instance-field layout dictionary: a second Awake is a no-op (`Destroy(this)`); the port now keeps that rule.
- World::Craft (the WP-14 route without KSPUpgradePipeline) accepts 33 of the 86 harness stock crafts; WP-18's route with the pipeline loads 57.
- `kspcore_tests -s` aborts in "WP-24 ModuleReactionWheel vs tools/wp24/sas_reference.py" (doctest's success reporter; the baseline binary too):
  run without `-s`.

### Risks

- R1: C6's pad case is a single value (the vessel is anchored for all 500 frames); a capture of the GoOffRails placement (vesselTransform before and
  after CheckGroundCollision) would pin the remaining 1.08 cm.
- R2: the stock crafts of the receiver case are those LoadShip accepts without the upgrade pipeline; renamed-part crafts are not covered.
